# Publisher's Preface.

The writings of the famous chemist <note>original Latin: "Chymici"</note>, Johannes Isaac Hollandus, have not only received exceptional acclaim for more than a century <note>original Latin: "Seculo"</note> among the masters and lovers of Hermetic philosophy <note>A tradition of spiritual and material alchemy named after the legendary Hermes Trismegistus.</note>, and been considered among the most excellent and perfect of their kind—thereby earning their author a great name and high esteem—but they have also remained, to this day, held in high value among all true connoisseurs, despite the large number of alchemical <note>original German: "alchymischer"</note> books that have appeared from time to time.

<summary>This preface introduces Johannes Isaac Hollandus as a preeminent figure in alchemy whose works have maintained their reputation and authority for over a hundred years.</summary>

<keywords>Johannes Isaac Hollandus, Hermetic philosophy, alchemy, history of chemistry, 18th-century publishing, alchemical literature</keywords>

## Publisher’s Preface.

The writings of the famous alchemist <note>original Latin: "Chymici." In the 18th century, the terms for chemist and alchemist were often used interchangeably, though here it specifically refers to a master of the Hermetic arts.</note>, Johannes Isaac Hollandus, have not only received exceptional acclaim for more than a century <note>original Latin: "Seculo."</note> among the masters and enthusiasts of **Hermetic Philosophy** <note>The tradition of spiritual and physical alchemy attributed to the legendary figure Hermes Trismegistus.</note>, and been considered among the most excellent and perfect of their kind—thereby earning their author a great name and high esteem—but they also remain to this day, despite the vast number of **alchemical books** which have appeared from time to time, held in high value by all true connoisseurs...

<summary>This preface introduces the works of Johannes Isaac Hollandus, emphasizing his long-standing reputation as a master of alchemy and the enduring value of his writings compared to other texts in the field.</summary>

Therefore, I consider it entirely superfluous to accompany the present collection with further words of praise; still less does it seem necessary to me to set forth, with many digressions, the motives <note>original German: "Beweg-Gründe"</note> which have prompted me to produce this new edition.

It is well known that these small works <note>original Latin: "Opuscula"</note> printed together here—which were already translated in the previous century <note>original Latin: "Seculo"</note> from various old Low German <note>The dialects spoken in Northern Germany and the Netherlands, which was the original language of Hollandus.</note> manuscripts into the High German <note>The standard literary German used in this 18th-century edition.</note> language, and were published in print from time to time in various places, some individually and others in smaller collections—have become very rare over the course of time due to the high demand for copies <note>original: "Exemplarien"</note>.

Chapter I. The first wrong path in the reading of false books, etc. 345–348.

<note>original: "De particularibus." In alchemical theory, a "particular" work is a recipe that produces a specific result—such as silvering a metal—but is not the "universal" transmutation achieved by the Stone.</note>

<note>original: "Cementir-Ofen." Cementation involved heating a metal together with a powdered chemical agent (the "cement") to refine the metal or alter its surface.</note>

<note>original: "Aquafort und Aqua Regis." Strong water (Aqua Fortis) is nitric acid; Royal Water (Aqua Regia) is a mixture of nitric and hydrochloric acid, famous for its ability to dissolve gold.</note>

<note>original: "Putrificir-Ofen." Putrefaction was the alchemical stage of decomposition or "rotting," often symbolized by the color black (nigredo), where the material was broken down to its basic components using gentle, moist heat.</note>

<note>original: "Digerir-Ofen." Digestion refers to the process of exposing a substance to consistent, gentle heat over a long period, mimicking the natural warmth of a stomach or a womb to "ripen" the material.</note>

<note>The "Great Elixir" is another name for the Philosopher's Stone, the universal medicine and catalyst for transmutation.</note>

<term>Quintessence: Literally the "fifth essence" (quinta essentia). In alchemy, it is the purest, most concentrated medicinal or spiritual core of a substance, extracted through repeated distillation.</term>

— XXVII. Preparing the matter with which gold is cemented. 454.

— XXVIII. <term>Sublimation</term> of mercury toward the Red. 455.

— XXIX. XXX. How to extract all <term>Tinctures</term>. 456. – 461.
<term>Tincture: An alchemical extract or concentrated liquid capable of "tinging" or transforming the color and quality of other substances, often used as a medicine or for transmutation.</term>

would have, although the reading of his printed books until now has not been able to bear as much fruit as it hopefully will do now. It consists in the author having had the flaw of saying a thing so often that it brings a greater annoyance to some to read it than it brought the author to write it so many times. If such *tautology* <note>original: "tautologia"; the unnecessary repetition of the same idea or word.</note> were purged from the author’s writings, many would much prefer to read them; I must myself confess that dealing with such things was very vexing for me. 

But the reader must know that there are all kinds of people, and thus also those to whom one can almost never say a thing too often; for them, what is said too much for lovers of brevity is still perhaps too little. # Preface.

for the Dutch give their children only one name, and also have no surname; rather, the father's first or baptismal name becomes the son's surname, with the addition of the word "sen" or "son." So, in the Dutch manner, the younger **Hollandus** was likely called **Jan Isaacsen**—that is, **Johannes Isaacsson**—which I thought not inappropriate to mention here. 

There are also several other treatises attributed to this our author, which are said to still exist, such as <term>On the Oil of Antimony</term> <note>original: "de oleo Stibii"; stibium is the Latin name for the element antimony, a key material in alchemy.</note>, which is without doubt the treatise that appears under the name of **Bacon** within the *Triumphal Chariot of Basil* <note>A reference to the *Triumph-Wagen Antimonii* (Triumphal Chariot of Antimony) by the legendary alchemist Basil Valentine. Should I obtain more, I do not wish to withhold it from the <term>lovers of the art</term> <note>original: "Liebhabern"; a term used for dedicated students or practitioners of alchemy.</note>. 

On the other hand, I ask and exhort others as well: if they possess or acquire good writings, they should measure for me with the same measure I use for them—that is, they should also allow them to be printed, so that we devotees may get to read them. This is in consideration of the fact that they were written by their authors for this purpose: that much good might be promoted thereby. things go this way, because it happened even to the Almighty Lord Jesus that all His labor benefited only the very few. Thus, as previously mentioned, even when they are not suppressed, good books cannot <term>effect</term> <note>original: "operiren"; from the Latin 'operari,' meaning to produce a result or work, often used in a medical or alchemical context.</note> much good—let alone if one intends to hide them away first, leaving them to the moths and worms. Such good books are rare enough as it is; by contrast, there is an abundance of useless ones. These are hatched annually like harmful <margin>handwritten mark</margin> vermin (under changed titles, but always playing the same old tune: "So writes Hippocrates, Galen, Luther, Augustine, the <term>Body of Law</term> <note>original: "Corpus Juris"; the foundational collection of Roman law used in universities.</note>, etc."). It is as if one could not read these authors for oneself, but required a thousand foolish repeaters instead—and then one is even expected to revere such people as great <term>Doctors</term> and <term>Licentiates</term> <note>A 'Licentiate' was an academic rank allowing one to practice a profession, sitting just below the rank of Doctor.</note> because of their lousy citations and hundredfold copying of other people’s books. 

The authors of these works are mostly in need of starting over as proper <term>disciples</term> <note>original: "Discipeln"; students or apprentices.</note> themselves, learning something righteous before they attempt to teach. Most, however, do the opposite: they leap from their childish youth straight into the rank of Doctor or the highest level of teacher. Since they cannot earn this through proper talent, they have themselves graduated for money—just as if common water could be made to pass for a magnificent wine by means of a false written certificate.

# Preface.

—which is exceedingly strange to hear, and yet it is in full swing not only in the world, but even throughout Christendom: that such young people are granted degrees for money. These are men who perhaps barely a few years ago were still attending common grammar schools; indeed, sometimes so little time has passed that the neighbors can still remember seeing them riding hobby-horses with other boys or engaged in other childish games. 

How, then, could the great art of acting as Doctors and writing voluminous books come to them so quickly? For, by all rights, such things require a special gift from God and many years of experience. And nonetheless, such books—devoid of any strength or substance <note>original: "Krafft und Safftlose"; literally "strength- and sap-less," describing books that lack genuine medicinal or intellectual vitality.</note>—are written in great heaps. 

Would to God that such works were withheld, and that instead the writings of those precious men—of whom barely one is seen in fifty or a hundred years—were most diligently promoted. How long has it been since Paracelsus <note>Philippus Aureolus Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim (1493–1541), a Swiss physician and alchemist who pioneered the use of chemicals and minerals in medicine.</note> lived, and yet we still do not possess his <term>Herbarium</term> <note>A book or treatise describing plants and their medicinal properties.</note>? Likewise, we still lack most of the works of the precious Carrichter <note>Bartholomäus Carrichter (c. 1510–1567), a famous physician to Emperors Maximilian II and Ferdinand I, whose botanical works were highly sought after.</note>, etc. 

But those who willfully withhold such treasures are nothing less than public thieves of the world, whoever they may be. But enough of this; I hereby commend the reader to God’s protection and the fulfillment of the Holy Spirit. 

Written in February 1667.

# Concerning the Hand of the Philosophers.

This is the Hand of the Philosophers with its seven secret signs, by which hand the ancient sages were bound and sworn to one another. No one can understand this hand with its secret signs, unless it be that he first becomes an initiate <note>German: *Geschworner*, referring to someone who has taken a formal oath of secrecy</note> of the philosophers, and has faithfully served them in the art of <term>Alchemy</term> <note>original: *Alchemia*</note>. Therefore, whoever does not possess this hand, and does not understand its secret signs, nor is faithfully sworn to it, such individuals are "bastards" <note>A term used for false alchemists or those working without the proper spiritual foundation</note> in this art; they shall not possess the treasure of the philosophers. For this reason, I advise all those who do not possess these secrets of the hand, that they should not set to work in the Alchemical art, nor believe the books and writings, since they will only be deceived regarding the secrets of the hand; therefore, let every person take good heed.

Within this hand is enclosed the secret of the philosophers, namely concerning the Seed and the Earth, as shall be reported hereafter.

## Preparation of Saltpeter.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration depicting a decorative crown with floral or fleur-de-lis points and jewels on its band. To the right of the crown is a small, textured square or basket-like object.</image-desc>

Take quicklime <note>original: *lebendigen Kalck*; calcium oxide used for its reactive properties</note>, according to the quantity of the substance, and pour a good portion of urine upon it. Let the lime be slaked <note>the process of adding liquid to quicklime to produce a chemical reaction</note> therein, and after it is slaked, let it settle. Pour off the clear liquid from the top. If there are 6 lbs. of saltpeter, take 12 lbs.—or *Seidel* <note>a historical liquid measure, roughly a pint</note>—of the clear urine, or even more, but not less. Put it together into a clean kettle; boil it well and skim it until fine and clear with an iron skimmer. Occasionally dip the skimmer into the liquor <note>original: *liquorem*</note> and splash it into the fire; if it burns or causes the coals to flare up, it is finished. Lift it down and let it cool slightly, then pour it into a large linen bag, like a straining bag <note>original: *Claresack*; used for clarifying liquids</note>. This bag should hang five feet high over a barrel. Then cones <note>original: *Zapffen*; referring to the needle-like crystal structures of potassium nitrate</note> will form in the water, one over the other, as if they were crystal. Take these out, for that is the purified saltpeter. Then take the other saltpeter which did not form into cones, fish it out, and put it into the urine; let it boil again as before—

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration of a tall, cylindrical chemical vessel or furnace, possibly representing the "Laterne" mentioned in the text. The apparatus has a domed lid with a small vent or knob at the top, a body marked with vertical lines, and a flat circular base.</image-desc>

Take a new earthenware pot with a lid that fits closely upon it. Pulverize enough <term>rock alum</term> <note>original: *Allaun de roche*; a naturally occurring potassium aluminum sulfate mineral used as a mordant and in chemical purifications</note> into it so that the pot is half-full. <term>Lute</term> <note>original: *lutirs*; the act of sealing a vessel's joints with a paste made of clay, lime, or other materials to make it airtight</note> it carefully so that no air may escape. Place it over a small fire and listen to the pot; when it no longer seethes, diminish your fire, and finally let the pot glow for one hour, and then let it cool. It is finished.

# Hand of the Philosophers #

Things composed and united from the four <term>Elements</term> <note>The four classical elements: Earth, Air, Fire, and Water.</note> which are <term>contrary</term> <note>original: "contrair." Alchemical theory held that elements with opposing qualities—like hot vs. cold or moist vs. dry—must be balanced to achieve stability.</note> have been put together by Him with their opposites; yet all these natures are perfectly united in all things, whether they be equally perfect or imperfect. And so we find in the same thing that what is manifest in it is perfect, or what is hidden in it is perfect. But in the coldness it is contrary; therefore it is easy to lead the <term>Bodies</term> <note>original: "Corpora." In this context, it refers to the physical forms of the metals.</note> back to their first root in a short time, <margin>//</margin> so that you may make manifest that which is hidden, and make hidden that which is manifest in the nature of the metals. <margin>|</margin> For what <term>Iron</term> <note>original: "Eisen," associated with the planet Mars.</note> lacks in its manifest state is compensated for in its hidden state; <margin>|</margin> for its manifest part is Iron, and it is compensated for when one compares it to <term>Gold</term> <note>original symbol: ☉</note> or <term>Silver</term> <note>original symbol: ☽</note>, and its hidden part is <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note>, which is compensated for in its comparison.

# Johann Isaac Hollandus #

Because there are many kinds of defects in the metals, you may well transmute the metals into another nature, and do so with <term>Sulfur</term><note>In alchemy, Sulfur represents the active, combustible, and "masculine" principle of matter, not just the common chemical element.</note>.

The other method is this: Take 1 pound of the powder and 1 pound of the Key; mix and sublime them, and proceed with them as in the instruction for Saturn.

### Another Method.

### Tincture of Sulfur

The art of extracting the **Quintessence** <term>Quinta Essentia</term><note>The "fifth essence" or purest, most medicinal core of a substance.</note> from **sulfur** <note>original symbol: "🜍".</note>, **orpiment** <term>Auripigment</term><note>A deep orange-yellow arsenic sulfide mineral.</note>, calcined **ochre** <term>Ochra</term>, **vitriol** <term>Atrament</term><note>A group of sulfate minerals, often used for making inks and acids.</note>, red **arsenic** <term>Arsenico</term>, or similar things, is all one way, art, or method, as follows.

In the event that you have any material and wish to extract the tincture from it, pulverize it until it is impalpable <note>A powder so fine it cannot be felt between the fingers.</note>. Pour <margin>M</margin><note>Likely an abbreviation for Menstruum, the alchemical term for a solvent.</note> old, clear urine upon it; let it boil until the urine is colored, then pour it off and pour more over it until all the tincture is extracted. Then evaporate all the colored urine, and to what remains at the bottom, pour vinegar over it and extract all the tincture with that as well. Whatever then remains on the bottom is useless, for it is the saltiness of the urine. Draw off the colored vinegar by means of a **water bath** <term>balneum</term>, and a most beautiful redness will remain at the bottom, which shines brighter than **gold** <note>original symbol: "☉" (Sol).</note> and seems to be a heavenly color. Dissolve this tincture in the "water of the hand" <note>This refers to the specific solvent or "mercury" associated with the "Hand of the Philosophers" described earlier in the manuscript.</note>, distill it off just like the previous tincture—by dissolving, distilling, congealing, and preparing it—to its highest degree and capability; or you may **sublimate** <note>The process of heating a substance until it becomes a vapor and then collects as a solid again, used for purification.</note> it by means of **Sal Ammoniac** <note>original symbol: "🜹". A crystalline salt used to help metals and minerals vaporize.</note>.

### Tincture of Antimony

Take **antimony** <note>original: "Antimonium". A naturally occurring mineral (stibnite) highly prized by alchemists for its purifying properties.</note> from the mines, pulverize it until it is impalpable <note>A powder so fine it cannot be felt between the fingers.</note>, and pour distilled vinegar over it in a glass or stone jar. Place it for six weeks in horse manure or in a **water bath** <term>balneum</term>, but the horse manure must be renewed every week; the longer [it sits], the better. Afterwards, place it in a flask with an **alembic** <note>The "helm" or cap of a still used to collect and condense vapors.</note>, draw the vinegar over with a boiling water bath, and then drive it [with higher heat] in a sand bath. Thus the blessed **Quintessence** <term>Quinta Essentia</term><note>The "fifth essence," or the purest, most medicinal core of a substance.</note> will sublimate <note>To heat a solid so that it turns into vapor and then back into a solid on a cooler surface, purifying it.</note> and come down the beak of the helm like drops of red blood. Collect these separately, take them off, and mix them with the "key" <note>An alchemical "key" is a specific reagent or solvent required to "unlock" or activate a substance.</note>, which should be prepared so dry that it turns to dust. Then distill it via a water bath with a small fire—one so gentle that you could just barely endure your hand in it—and let it stand to distill for 21 days, or until it gives off no more moisture. Then congeal <note>Turn from a liquid into a solid state.</note> two ounces <note>original symbol: "℥ii".</note> of the Quintessence, and furthermore all moist spirits, so that you may sublimate them. Then move it from the water bath into the sand [bath] to sublimate the two ounces of the red Quintessence, which is a heavenly, incombustible redness.

### A Stone of the Philosophers.

Take <note>original: "℞", the traditional recipe symbol for "recipe" or "take."</note> 1 ounce of fine **Silver** <note>original: "☽", the symbol for the Moon/Silver.</note> and dissolve it in common **Aqua Fortis** <note>original: "AF". Grind this mercury very fine upon a hard stone, let it dissolve there by itself <note>This likely refers to deliquescence, where a salt absorbs enough moisture from the air to turn into a liquid.</note>, then coagulate it again over a small fire in a glass, and grind it again as before, and dissolve it as before for 7 times; cast 1 ounce of this elixir upon 31 ounces of prepared, well-flowing copper, and you will have fine silver in all tests.

### To make Venus fixed.

Take soap <note>Early modern alchemists often used soap as a source of alkaline salts in their processes.</note> and dry it until it no longer smokes, then apply high heat until it becomes lime <note>original: "Kalck". In alchemy, this refers to a powder produced by heating a substance to extreme temperatures, a process called calcination.</note>, and plug it at the top with a stone when you calcine; to this take an equal amount of verdigris <term>Spanisch grüne</term> and seal it in a crucible, lute it shut tightly <note>original: "lutirs geheb zu". To lute is to seal a vessel with a specialized clay or paste to make it airtight.</note>, place it in the fire for two hours, and melt it; thus you have fixed and malleable **Venus** <note>original: "♀", the astrological and alchemical symbol for Copper. "Fixed" means the metal has been rendered resistant to heat and will no longer evaporate or change easily.</note>.

### Mercury transforms all metallic bodies with Arsenic into Silver, and with Sulfur into Gold.

Take a thick cloth and bind the **Mercury** in it, hang it over a pot containing sulfur, then, with the pot fired from below and sealed, it will congeal <note>original: "congeliren". To change from a liquid or vaporous state into a solid.</note> into red; but if one rubs this Mercury with alkaline salt <term>Sal alcali</term> and white lead <term>Cerussa</term>, it becomes white. Conversely, when one rubs it with water from the **Saffron of Mars** <term>Croco ♂</term> <note>original symbol: ♂ for Mars or Iron. Saffron of Mars is a name for iron oxide.</note>, **Vitriol** <note>original symbol: 🜵</note>, and **Atrament** <note>A term used for various dark, metallic salts, usually ferrous sulfate.</note>, it nonetheless remains red; one also congeals it with **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃", the symbol for Tin.</note> in a sealed vessel. With **Saturn** <note>original: "Saturno", symbol: ♄ for Lead.</note>, one congeals Mercury in white works <note>The "white work" (albedo) is the stage of alchemy aimed at producing silver.</note>, enclosed in a pipe or other vessel and luted with the **clay of wisdom** <term>luto sapientiæ</term> <note>A specialized sealant used by alchemists, often made of clay, horsehair, and other binding agents.</note>; and if this is thrown upon molten Saturn and thus held in the fire, it will be congealed by the smoke of Saturn.

### Concerning Gold and Mercury. ###

Here begins a very magnificent work regarding the Sun <note>original: "$\odot$"; gold</note> and Mercury <note>original: "$\text{\}$"; quicksilver</note>, how to join and unite them, and also how to fix <note>to make a volatile substance stable under heat</note> them together into the very best gold.

This water is of two kinds: one for the Red and the other for the White <note>the "Red" and "White" refer to the final stages of the Great Work, creating the solar/gold or lunar/silver tinctures</note>. To this, take 1 lb. of <term>spirit of wine</term> <note>original: "Aqua vitæ"</note>, 1 lb. of coarse unrefined salt, and let them boil together. But take care that you do not put your matter into lead-glazed pots

Then, put it back into the mortar and rub it once more with the same water as before. # Hand of the Philosophers.

Exaltation <note>original: "Exaltatio"; the process of raising a substance to a higher dignity or more potent state</note> of the spirit is the liquefaction <note>original: "liquefactio"; the process of turning a solid into a liquid</note> of the bodies.

The salts <note>original: "Salien"</note> of the bodies are made in many ways.

Solution <note>original: "Solutio"</note> is melting, or perhaps also pounding.

Calcination <note>original: "Calcinatio"</note> is the process of "making lime" <note>reducing a metal to a fine powder or oxide through heat</note>, and it happens in sand with a strong fire in order to consume the foul sulfur <note>alchemists believed "foul sulfur" was the combustible impurity that caused metals to corrode or be "imperfect"</note> out of a thing; for when such sulfur is consumed, the body remains pure in the lime <note>original: "Kalck"; the oxidized powder</note>; following this is inceration.

Inceration <note>original: "Inceratio"</note> is a refinement of the calxes, so that moisture may better permeate the bodies; inceration is nothing other than grinding and soaking until the material becomes like wax, so that one may easily dissolve or melt it with a small and gentle fire.

Dissolution <note>original: "Dissolutio"</note> is an unbinding <note>the release of the spirit from the physical form</note>, which is performed on the bodies that have been calcined, and it is carried out thus: put the material you wish to dissolve into a glass and stop it up well at the top, and cover it with moist earth, and lay horse manure <note>Pferde-Mist; used in laboratories as a source of steady, gentle "living" heat through fermentation</note> upon it, which has been well-sprinkled with water, and let it stand thus for 7 days; on the 8th day it should dissolve, and this is dissolution by heat. But dissolution by cold moisture is when you make a ledge <note>original: "Kante"; likely a shelf or pit in a cool, damp cellar</note> and place therein a glazed vessel with a little water at the bottom; let the glass hang over the water, yet so that it does not touch the water, and the glass vessel

Cover the vessel with a lid, but place wax upon the glass and sand upon the wax; let it remain thus for an entire day and night, and so it will dissolve <note>original: "dissolviren"; the process of a solid turning into a liquid state</note>.

**Coagulation** <note>original: "Coagulatio"</note> is a hardening <note>original: "Hartmachung"</note>, and it occurs in this manner: take the aforementioned glass containing the material that has been dissolved, place it in a cupel <note>original: "Test"; a shallow, porous vessel used in assaying or refining</note> with sifted ashes, and build a fire under the cupel for 10 hours, or for as long as it takes until the moisture has departed; then it will look like minium <note>original: "Mini"; red lead (lead tetroxide), used here as a color reference</note>; if, however, it is intended for the "white work," it will look like a very white camphor.

**Rubification of sal ammoniac** <note>original: "Rubificatio salis Armeniaci"; the process of turning ammonium chloride red</note>: take <term>sal ammoniac</term> <note>⚹ / Ammonium chloride</note> and <term>crocus of Mars</term> <note>♂ / Iron oxide powder</note> in equal parts, well-powdered and mixed together; put this into a glass and pour good distilled wine-vinegar over it to a height of three fingers; let it stand thus for a day and night, stirring it well at all times; then let it dry out gently over a soft fire. Following this, put the <term>sal ammoniac</term> and the <term>crocus of Mars</term> into a sublimatory <note>original: "Sublimatorium"; a vessel used to heat a substance until it vapors and then solidifies again at the top</note> and sublimate it; it will rise to the top as red as blood. Even if the vinegar was not distilled, it does not matter; it amounts to the same thing.

**Rubification of Roman Vitriol** <note>original: "Rubificatio Vitrioli Romani"; Roman vitriol usually refers to iron sulfate or copper sulfate</note>: graduate <note>original: "gradir"; to refine or increase the potency or color of a substance</note> it and calcine <note>original: "calcinir"; reduce to a powder through high heat</note> it in a great fire, and it will become as red as blood.

# Here follow three more treatises by Isaac Hollandus.

<note>Isaac Hollandus and his son John Isaac Hollandus were legendary figures in late medieval and early modern alchemy; their writings were highly influential for their clear, though often difficult, laboratory instructions.</note>

### The First: To make an Elixir from urine.

<note>Urine was a significant substance in early chemistry (alchemy) as a source of various salts and, eventually, phosphorus.</note>

### The second speaks of another type of Alchemy, or what is called the Great Elixir.

### The third is about the *Irir* of the Ancients.

<note>The term "Irir" is likely a variation or transcription error for "Iris" (the rainbow), referring to the *cauda pavonis* or peacock's tail stage of the alchemical process where many colors appear, or possibly a specific preparation of "Iiris" (Orris) or a corruption of "Elixir."</note>

The art of alchemy consists of three things: namely, in "Our Stone," which is the free art of the ancients and their successors, who shall discover this free art through <term>science</term> <note>original: "Scienz"; theoretical or systematic knowledge</note> or through <term>practice</term> <note>original: "Practic"; experimental laboratory work</note>; or to whom the Holy Spirit gives it, or bestows it through His illumination. Blessed is he who possesses this free art and applies it well to the glory of God and for the needs of his neighbor.

The second type of alchemy is the **Elixir**, which is prepared as the ancients taught, from the "Hand of the Philosophers" <note>This refers to the "Hand of the Philosophers," a famous mnemonic diagram attributed to Hollandus that uses the fingers and palm to map out alchemical ingredients and steps</note>. Those who possess this and understand it well may also be called blessed.

The art of alchemy has many more daughters, branches, and roots, which spring from these three trees I have just mentioned; that is: that some labor with great effort in the <term>calcining</term> <note>original: "Calciniren"; the process of heating a substance to high temperatures in the presence of air to reduce it to a powder or oxide</note> of <term>bodies</term> <note>original: "Cörper"; in an alchemical context, this refers to the seven base metals</note>, in order to wash them and make them pure and clean; others with <term>amalgamations</term> <note>original: "amalgamarionibus"; the process of softening or dissolving a metal by mixing it with mercury</note>; others with whitening, <term>cementing</term> <note>original: "cementiren"; a dry refining process used to purify gold</note>, augmenting, or <term>reddening</term> <note>original: "rubificiren"; the process of bringing the alchemical work to the final red stage, or "rubedo"</note>. Others make salts from the bodies or metals. Others make oils, and other works with the bodies in the fire: others with <term>strong waters</term> <note>original: "aquis fortibus"; mineral acids, most commonly nitric acid, used to dissolve and separate metals</note>, others with salts upon the bodies: and so forth in many manners; and it is all good, when it is done rightly, as the ancestors taught, but all this is achieved with great labor.

Whoever has now wedded one among these daughters will indeed never suffer want again, but one must bring it about with great labor and care, and it would indeed be necessary that every good and experienced alchemist should have all these daughters in marriage—that is, that he should well know and understand all these operations, so that he might distinguish between good and evil; but enough of that, etc.

# John Isaac Hollandus #

In all the world, I know of nothing that would be so good and healthy for our nature as this divine **Philosophers' Stone**.

Now we wish to report again in what manner we must prepare our **Stone**, which is at hand as a **dead body** <term>original: "todt Corpus"; a material substance purged of its original qualities</term>, yet it is glorified and made pure, and fit to house the **spirit of life** and the **perfect soul** within it, and to make them eternal.

If you wish to make this **Stone** living, you may bring it to whatever **corpse** <term>original: "Leichnam"; used here to mean a material "body" or base substance</term> you wish; you can make from it a **Philosophers' Stone** <term>original: "Lapidem Philosophorum"</term> or **Quintessence** <term>original: "Qu. Ess." or "Quinta Essentia"; the purest, most concentrated essence of a substance</term>, all of which maintain and preserve the human body in full health without any decline of the body, until the final term of each person's life, as was heard above. However, if you wish to make it into a **Medicine** for **impure metals** <note>base metals like lead or tin, which alchemists viewed as "diseased" versions of gold</note>, then you must guide it toward metals, for a horse begets a horse, etc. <note>An alchemical axiom: like produces like; to create a metallic result, one must use metallic principles.</note>

Furthermore, to reach our purpose, my child shall take **mercury** <term>original symbol: ☿</term> which is dissolved in **nitric acid** <term>original: "Af." or "Aqua Fortis"</term> and sublimate it four or five times through **vitriol** <term>sulfate minerals</term> and **salt**; the more one sublimates it, the greater its **projection** <term>the final stage of alchemy where the Stone is cast upon base metals to transform them into gold</term> becomes. Following this, rub the mercury thus sublimated into a powder upon a stone, and place it in a wide vessel one thumb's width thick, and set it in a **tripod** <term>a stand for heating vessels</term> to **calcine** <term>to reduce to a powder through prolonged heating</term> for eight days, though with a gentle coal fire, such that you [could say] an **Hail Mary** <note>original: "Ave Maria"; the author uses the duration of a prayer as a traditional measurement of time or to indicate a specific low heat</note>

### Johann Isaac Hollandus ###

...as I taught you before, that you should take much more spirit <term>spiritus; the volatile, liquid component</term> than you have of the body <term>corpus; the solid matter</term>. And now, in this sublimation <term>the process of heating a substance until it vaporizes and then solidifies again, used to purify or concentrate matter</term>, the body will let go of the spirit if it has too much of it. Let it stand in the pot over the fire for 3 days and nights with a steady fire, as is proper for sublimation; then take the pot down and take out the Stone. 

Test it on a glowing copper plate <note>original: "kupffernen glüenden Lameln"</note> and see if it melts like wax and spreads out upon the plate, penetrating into it like lard into dry leather. After the plate has cooled, if the spot where the Stone spread is good gold in all tests, then your Stone is precious and already finished and perfected. 

But if it does not do this, then you must dissolve it again in strong water <term>Af.; abbreviation for aqua fortis or nitric acid</term> and place it again in Mary's Bath <term>Balneum Mariæ; a vessel of water used to heat a substance gently and indirectly</term> for 7 days, and then congeal <term>congeliren; to solidify or thicken</term> it again. Take it out and let it stand again for 8 days in the tripod <term>tripode; a three-legged stand or furnace used for sustained heating</term> as before. Then take it out and test it as before; and the more you dissolve and congeal it, the greater its power of projection <term>projectio; the final stage of alchemy where the Stone is cast upon base metal to transmute it</term> will be. 

If the Stone acts as one part upon 100, and you dissolve and congeal it again, it shall achieve a tenfold higher projection. But I advise you that you only do it 3 times, for the Stone would reach such high power and subtlety <term>subtilität; here meaning a refined, penetrating quality</term> that it could be kept in no kind of vessel, so penetrating would it be. Therefore, I advise you to do it only 3 times...

### Another method that is easier. ###

<margin>URINE</margin> Take our Stone in its coarseness <term>crudity; the raw, unrefined state of the material</term>, just as it comes from the human mine <note>original: *des Menschen Minera*; a common alchemical euphemism for urine, which Hollandus believed contained the "Stone"</note>—understand well what I am saying—put it into a wide glass bowl, and then also put the beaten gold <note>original: represented by the symbol $\odot$</note> leaves into it. Then pour in some of our Stone which is old, matured, and purified; pour the Stone two fingers high over the gold, and set the bowl with the gold and the Stone in the heat of the summer sun. 

Then a white, golden film or oil will rise to the top; take that off cleanly from the top with a small feather, in such a way that you move the material as little as you can. Do this several times a day by removing the oil, until no more oil rises up. In this way, you can obtain the Oil of Gold <note>original: *Oleum Solis*</note> with our Stone in its coarseness, just as it comes from the human mine. 

Listen well to what I have indicated to you here, for there was never a greater secret in nature than our Stone, in that even in its coarseness it transforms gold into oil. Many artists <note>In this context, "artists" refers to practicing alchemists</note> have sought this but did not find it; therefore, be grateful to God. Now, if our Stone does this in its raw state <note>original: *Crudität*</note>, consider what it will do once it is perfected <note>original: *perficiret*</note> and united with the Spirit and Soul, and is fixed, subtle, and fusible. Just reflect well upon my words so that you do not perform wasted labor.

Your gold <term>$\odot$</term> or silver <term>$\leftmoon$</term> will then be brittle or crumbly, since too much Medicine <note>another term for the Stone or elixir</note> has been applied to it. For this is the test of Elixirs: if one wishes to perform Projection <term>the act of casting the alchemical agent onto molten base metal to transform it</term> with something, but does not know the exact ratio for the Projection, then throw your Medicine onto whichever metal you wish. As long as the metal remains brittle, your Medicine is still capable of an even higher degree of Projection. Thus, continue to throw that brittle metal onto other metals until the metals remain ductile <note>original: *geschmeidig*; meaning the metal is no longer brittle and can be hammered without breaking, signaling the transmutation is complete and balanced</note>, etc. Keep this in mind, for that is the limit of the Projection. I have said that you should throw 1 lb. of the Stone onto 10 lbs. of gold <term>$\odot$</term>.

In this way, you bring the gold or silver to such a degree of subtlety that it is unbelievable, and the power of <term>projection</term> <note>the final step where the Stone is cast upon base metal to transform it into gold</note> will increase infinitely.

Furthermore, we wish to indicate what preparations we must make with the bodies, that is, with our <term>Stone</term> <note>the Philosopher's Stone or the Great Elixir</note>. After we have prepared it to be clear and subtle, our duty requires us to dissolve it in strong water, and to place it, well-sealed, into the water bath to <term>putrefy</term> <note>original: "putrificiren"; a stage of breaking down and "rotting" the substance to release its inner essence</note> for as long as we wish—though the longer, the better.

## The Third Kind of Alchemy, Called Ixir.

I will now continue to briefly discuss the <term>Ixir</term>, which is the third pillar upon which Alchemy stands, as I mentioned at the beginning of this book. You should know that one may certainly make an <term>Ixir</term> from our <term>Stone</term> <note>The Philosopher's Stone</note>. For where the <term>soul, spirit, and body</term> <note>The three essential components of all matter: Sulfur, Mercury, and Salt</note> are not joined together as is proper, nor <term>fixed</term> <note>original: "figiret"; rendered stable and non-volatile so the substance does not evaporate when heated</note> with one another, such things are collectively called <term>Ixirs</term>, which are not perfected. However, where <term>soul, body, and spirit</term> are composed together as is fitting, and are fixed with one another and also made <term>fusible</term> <note>Able to be melted</note>—all of those are <term>Elixirs</term> and are good for eternity. The <term>Elixir</term> <note>The most refined alchemical substance, capable of transforming any base metal</note> transmutes all impure metals into fine gold and silver without any help from other things. Otherwise, you will go astray; take good heed of this, etc.

# Translator’s Preface.

Although, beloved reader, the noble little book by Hollandus, titled the *Work on Saturn* <note>original: "Opus Saturni"; Saturn is the alchemical name for lead</note>, is already found printed within Basil Valentine’s *Triumphal Chariot* <note>Referring to the *Triumphal Chariot of Antimony*, a foundational alchemical text attributed to the legendary monk Basilius Valentinus</note>, I have nevertheless desired to include it here with these other writings of his. This is for the reason that Hollandus himself writes therein that this work of his belongs not to the Mineral Work <note>original: "Opere Minerali"</note>, but rather to the Vegetable Work <note>original: "Opere Vegetabili," a branch of alchemy focused on extracting essences and salts from organic matter like plants</note>, and is the beginning and principal part of the *Vegetable Book*. 

Furthermore, in this *Work on Saturn*, he cites his subsequent Vegetable writings; thus, it seems appropriate to me that they follow one another here, so that one may explain the other and they may be compared. Additionally, the version of the *Work on Saturn* already in print is translated very much according to the Dutch <note>original: "Niederländischen"</note> style of speech, which at times uses words or idioms unintelligible to High Germans. I have therefore applied myself to [refine] this and that for the [high-] <note>The text ends here with a catchword "hoch-," indicating the sentence continues on the next page, likely referring to "High Germans."</note>

<summary>In this preface, the translator explains that although Johann Isaac Hollandus's work on lead (Saturn) was previously published elsewhere, it is included here because it serves as the essential introduction to his "Vegetable" or plant-based alchemical system. The translator also notes he has updated the language from a Dutch-influenced dialect to a clearer High German style.</summary>

### Chapter I.

Let it be known to my child that the stone, which one calls the <term>Philosophers’ Stone <note>original Latin: "Lapidem Philosophorum"</note></term>, has its origin from <term>Saturn <note>The alchemical name for lead, associated with the god and planet of the same name</note></term>, and for these reasons [or for this reason it has the name <term>Philosophers’ Stone</term>] once it has been perfected, it performs <term>projection <note>original: "projection"; the alchemical act of casting a small amount of the Stone onto a base metal to transmute it into gold, or applying it to the body as a universal cure</note></term> (general cures) both in the human body against all ailments that may afflict a person internally and externally, whatever they may be or be called, as well as in the imperfect metals. ### Chapter 2.

My child, lock this in your heart and understanding: namely, that this same Saturn is the very <term>Stone <note>The Philosopher's Stone</note></term> which the <term>philosophers <note>The historical term for alchemists</note></term> do not wish to make known by name. ### Chapter 20.

Therefore, take, in the name of God, twenty parts of **Saturn** <note>Lead, the primary metal used in this particular alchemical operation.</note> (compared to the one part that remained back in the fixation-glass) which has been prepared through **dissolving and congealing** <note>A repetitive process of purification where the substance is turned to liquid and then solidified to remove impurities.</note> until it no longer throws off any dregs, as was mentioned at the beginning. Then, increase the fire **gradually** <note>original: "gradatim"</note> until the material turns yellow; the longer it remains, the yellower it will become, until it reaches perfect **yellowness** <note>original: "Citrinität" — a traditional stage in the alchemical "Great Work" signifying maturity of the material.</note>. ## Translator’s Preface to the Vegetable Work.

Friendly, well-beloved reader, I have no doubt that it is well known to you and all <term>devotees<note>original: "Liebhabern"; in this context, it refers to "amateurs" or dedicated students of the hermetic arts</note></term> of natural secrets, how intensely for a long time now—yes, without doubt since the time when his writings first came to light, whether during the lifetime of Hollandus or shortly after his death—the aforementioned Hollandus's as-yet unpublished works have been sought after. This is especially true of his <term>Vegetable Work<note>original: "Opere Vegetabili"; the branch of alchemy dealing with the distillation and fermentation of plants and wine</note></term>, which he himself cites everywhere. Everyone is of the firm conviction that nothing of this work has yet reached the public domain, but that it has either already perished, or is perhaps being withheld by envious people <margin>withheld</margin>—

# Preface.

Furthermore, I wish to inform the reader that a manuscript was sent to me, along with a report stating it was copied from **Hollandus’s** <note>referring to Isaac Hollandus or his son, 15th-century Dutch alchemists whose works were widely circulated in the 17th century</note> own hand. At the beginning of that manuscript was the following **preface** <note>original: "Præfation"</note> by the author, followed by the **Mineral Works** <note>original: "Opera Mineralia"</note> and this **Vegetable Work** <note>original: "Opus Vegetabile," a treatise on obtaining alchemical essences from plants and wine</note>. However, because no proper order is maintained within that manuscript, I cannot know for certain to which work such a preface actually belongs, or if there is perhaps another book by the author (as I am not unaware that he also wrote a secret **Practical Application of the Philosophical Work** <term>Practicam Operis Philosophici: a technical manual for the laboratory operations required to create the Philosopher's Stone</term>, which I have not yet seen) which he perhaps introduced with this preface. Nevertheless, because the aforementioned preface by Hollandus fits well with the **Vegetable Work**, I have chosen to insert it before that text, hoping to do the reader a favor. In closing, I sincerely commend the reader to **Divine Grace, Enlightenment, and Blessing.**

### Hollandus’s Preface.

My child, you should know as time passes that God the Almighty Lord created the heavens and everything within them, and the world and all that is in it, as it is written in the Book of Genesis; and that the **first matter** <term>Prima Materia: the primitive, formless base of all matter in alchemical theory, often identified with the "waters" of Genesis</term> was water, upon which the Spirit of the Lord rested. # The First Part
### of the
# Vegetable Stone
## from Wine
## by ISAAC HOLLANDUS.

### Chapter 1.

In order to arrive at such a **Medicine** <note>In alchemical literature, the "Medicine" refers to the Philosopher's Stone in its medicinal capacity, capable of healing both metals and the human body.</note>, which cures and takes away all diseases, and keeps the healthy in a state of health, and drives away [the infirmities of] old age, and maintains the body in good condition until the final term of one’s life as it is set by GOD the Almighty; it is first of all things necessary to recognize the **Four Elements** <term>Elements: The fundamental building blocks—Earth, Water, Air, and Fire—whose balance was thought to determine the properties of all substances.</term> <note>original: *4. Elementa*</note>, and their nature in their internal and external aspects, their power and their **dregs** <term>Dregs: The waste or solid residue remaining after a distillation or extraction.</term> <note>original: *Feces*</note>, as well as what is contained within them; for therein are two natures, one that is perishable and [one that is] eternal; <note>The original German says "one that is perishable and eternal." In this context, it refers to the alchemical belief that matter contains both a corruptible physical part and an eternal, spiritual essence.</note> Therefore, it is necessary that we first have knowledge of the elements, since everything that is in the world has originated from and is composed of the **Four Elements**. Therefore, my child <note>Hollandus traditionally addresses the reader as "my child," establishing a father-son or master-apprentice relationship common in "Hermetic" teaching.</note> should know,

## Chapter 2.

<margin>213</margin>My child, let it be known to you that this Divine Medicine consists of three forms of knowledge, and in three manual works <term>Manual works: The physical laboratory operations or 'hand-work' required to produce the substance.</term> <note>original: *Hände-Wercken*</note>, and they have 3 distinct names, which are nonetheless all one; just as the **Holy Trinity** <note>original: *Heil. Dreyfaltigkeit*</note> consists of three distinct persons, who indeed have three distinct names, such as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit; the Father is not the Son, and the Son is not the Father, or the Holy Spirit; likewise, the Holy Spirit is neither Father nor Son, but each is a distinct person, and yet these 3 distinct persons are one essence, and in one power, and one strength. So it is also with these 3 different medicines: one is not the other, and although they are 3 different types, they are nonetheless one in essence, and of equal nature and power, with three different names, namely: **Vegetable, Animal, and Mineral**. By the **Vegetable** <note>original: *Vegetabilisch*</note> you must understand everything that grows out of the earth, such as herbs, trees, spices, fruits, and everything that sprouts from the earth, such as roots, flowers, and the like. The other is called **Animal** <note>original: *Animalisch*</note>, which is everything that [has] life...

...[li]fe and sensation within it, such as humans, animals, cattle, birds, fish, worms, and everything that has received life <note>original: *Leben*</note>. The third name is **Mineral**, namely everything that grows within the earth, such as gold, silver, and all metals, minerals, marcasites <term>Marcasites: In historical alchemy, this was a broad category for metallic ores and sulfides like pyrite, which were often considered "immature" or "unfinished" metals.</term>, stones, and everything that comes from the mines <note>original: *Mineren*</note>. These are three distinct names and three special natures in essence, differentiated into three distinct substances; nonetheless, when they are brought to their highest power—for which God created them—they shall be one in nature, remaining of equal power and essence throughout eternity, as shall be taught hereafter (if God wills).

### Chapter 3.

Above all things, my child should have the knowledge that **water** was created first, and into such water God incorporated His **earth**, and from the earth all things have sprouted; and everything that has received its essence and life has grown through the will of God with the assistance of the celestial bodies <note>original: *obern Cörpern*, literally "upper bodies"</note>, such as the Sun, Moon, Planets, and Stars. These collectively distribute their **influence** <term>Influence: In the worldview of the time, stars and planets were believed to "flow" their power into the earth, physically shaping the growth of plants and the formation of minerals.</term> and power over it, in the manner that God has provided through His Divine Order, as shall be explained in the text that follows.

### Chapter 4.

Furthermore, there are two manifest **Elements**, namely **Water** and **Earth**, within which two others are hidden: **Air** and **Fire**. These are influencing elements <note>original: *influirende Elementa*. In alchemical theory, these elements act as the active "influencers" that move through the more passive "manifest" elements.</note>. Air is contained within the Water, and Fire within the Earth; they are so tightly bound together that they can never truly be separated. Also, Earth and Fire are **fixed** <term>Fixed: A substance that remains stable and does not evaporate or change when exposed to high heat.</term>, while the other two, Water and Air, are **volatile** <term>Volatile: In alchemy, a substance that easily evaporates or "flies" away when heated.</term>. Therefore, the Water and the Air rise up, while the Earth and Fire remain together at the bottom. Among these four elements, Fire and Water are contrary <note>original: *widerwärtig*, meaning they naturally oppose or repel one another.</note> to each other. Air, however, harmonizes <note>original: *symphoniret*</note> or aligns with Fire in its heat, and with Water in its moisture. Likewise, Water harmonizes with Earth in its coldness, and Earth shares a similarity with Fire in its dryness. From this it clearly appears that every element accords <note>original: *concordiret*</note> with two other elements, and in one quality stands contrary <note>original: *contrariet*</note> or opposite to another.

### Chapter 6.

<margin>Note well</margin> <note>original Latin abbreviation: *NB* for *Nota Bene*</note>
My child should know that there are two kinds of water: one is the water from clouds, seas, or streams, and the other is the Elemental Water. This latter one is accounted as the true Element of Water and is the Water of the Philosophers <note>The "Philosophers" refers to alchemists; their "water" is a purified, essential substance rather than the common liquid found in nature.</note>, which the ignorant do not recognize. Likewise, there is an Earth that is white, pure, shining, and eternal; that is the Earth of the Philosophers. Alongside it, there is another: a black, stinking, and combustible earth. Furthermore, there is an Elemental Fire, which is eternal and is the Fire of the Philosophers; on the other hand, there is another fire which is combustible <note>i.e., common fire that consumes fuel and eventually goes out.</note>. In the same way, there is an Air which is elemental and is the Air of the Philosophers; alongside it, there is also a stinking and combustible air. Now, these are mixed together and among one another in such a way, and this is the reason why all things in the world are so easily destroyed, so that no thing [remains] long...

### Chapter 7.

Now I want to teach my child how he should separate the eternal elemental nature from this perishable nature; I will also make known to him what harm they <note>The corruptible elements</note> cause to people, cattle, and animals. To arrive at such a thing, however, which is harmless to nature, necessity demands, above all else, to learn in what manner we must separate that which is eternal from the perishable, stinking, and combustible. 

Hereupon it serves my child to know that in the separation of the elements there is much error, for many ignorant people are found who place herbs and plant species into putrefaction <term>Putrefaction: The process of decay or fermentation used in alchemy to break down a substance's physical form and release its internal "spirit."</term> and claim that they want to separate the elements from them in this way: When they have taken them out of the putrefaction, they draw the water off from them by means of a water bath <note>original Latin: *per balneum*—referring to the *balneum Mariae*, a gentle heating method using water</note> or by the fire; then they take out the matter from which the water was distilled and grind <note>original: *reiben*—literally "to rub," as with a mortar and pestle</note> it with its own water, and then set it to distill again over the fire, so a yellow water comes over, which they separate using a water bath, so the water comes away clear, and the yellow matter remains at the bottom <note>original Latin: *in fundo*</note> and will not rise in the water bath; they say this is the Element of Air, and

...they do not know what they are saying, since it is only some impurity from the fire and air which has risen with the water during distillation because of the stronger heat of the fire used for it. Then they take that which remained at the bottom of the pot and rub <note>original: *reiben*—referring to grinding with a mortar and pestle</note> it with its own water, and set it for six or seven days in <term>putrefaction</term> <note>Putrefaction: The process of allowing a substance to rot or ferment to break down its structure.</note>. Afterward, they distill it again over the fire, and a red, thick, and fatty matter comes over, which they call the element of Fire. They then separate this in a <term>water bath</term> <note>original Latin: *balneo*—specifically the *balneum Mariae*, a gentle heating method using hot water.</note>; the water comes away from it, and the red fatty matter remains at the bottom and will not rise out of the water bath. They take this out and then claim that they possess the element of Fire. Then they <term>calcine</term> <note>Calcine: To burn a substance to ashes at high heat to extract its mineral salts.</note> that which remained at the bottom of the pot and extract the salt from the <note>original Latin: *fecibus*—the dregs or solid remains.</note> dregs. Yet they do not know what they are saying or doing; they understand neither themselves nor the work they have performed, for they have no true knowledge of the elements. The proof of this is as follows: First, they set the matter to putrefy and rot, but the external heat—arising from the putrefaction or the water bath in which it stands—drives the internal natural warmth out of the thing they are putrefying. For the natural warmth that a thing possesses within itself is a spirit...

### Chapter 8.

After a thing has now come to its highest growth, it is then at its supreme power; subsequently, it begins to descend and decrease in taste, smell, and color, until the thing perishes. Finally, these three spirits depart from it entirely, and as soon as they are out of it, the thing (whether it be **vegetable** or **animal**) is dead, becomes foul-smelling, and rots. The very same happens in **putrefaction** <term>putrefaction</term> <note>The alchemical process of "death" and decomposition, intended to break down a substance to release its internal essence.</note>; what they <note>Referring to alchemical practitioners.</note> put into it is indeed living and good, but when they take it out again, they are rid of these three spirits, and the matter is dead, stinking, and rotten.

### Chapter 9.

Yet none of these three spirits are of the **elemental element** <note>The author distinguishes between the raw physical elements (Earth, Air, Fire, Water) and the divine "spirits" of life that inhabit them.</note>; rather, God has adorned and clothed the elements with these three spirits, and they are their life and soul.

Then they set this to distill in the **water bath** <term>Balneo</term> <note>From the Latin *balneum Mariae*, a vessel of hot water used to provide gentle, even heat to a flask, much like a modern double boiler.</note> and draw off its own water. They then grind that which remains at the bottom with its own water and set it again to putrefy in **dung** <note>original: *Mist*—decomposing horse manure was used in early laboratories as a natural source of steady, low "living" heat for weeks at a time.</note> or in the water bath for seven or eight days, or even ten or more, so that if any goodness from these three spirits might still—

->N 3<-

...it is known that one cannot separate the element of **Air** from the element of **Water**. One can, however, separate Water from the **Earth**; but as for **elemental Water**, **elemental Air**, and **elemental Fire**—these three no one in the world can separate from one another except for **GOD** alone, who has the power and no one else, because they are united and **betrothed** <note>original: *getrauet*. In alchemical philosophy, the elements are often described as being in a "marriage" or "betrothal" to signify their chemical and spiritual bonding.</note> to such an extent that they may not be separated, neither now nor in eternity. 

Certainly, one can separate from them the "water of the clouds," which is moist and flowing water, as well as all **corruption** <note>original: *Corruption*. Here referring to the impurities or decaying matter within a substance.</note> and **dregs** <term>Feces</term> <note>original: *Feces*. In an alchemical context, this refers to the solid residue, sediment, or waste products left over after a process like distillation or fermentation.</note> that are mixed therein, so that one may bring the elements to **crystalline clarity**; but the three elements—Air, Water, and Fire—are inseparable. The ignorant cannot grasp this: that no fire can exist without air, for if the air were drawn out of the fire, the heat of the fire would have to suffocate, die, and come to nothing. Also, if fire were withdrawn from the air, it would be purely water, for air is warm and moist and **participates** <note>In the sense of sharing properties or qualities.</note> with both water and fire; so, if the fire were drawn out of it, it would be pure water; and if the water were drawn out of the air, it would be pure fire. In such a way, you can easily come to understand that the aforementioned three elements are inseparable. To be sure, one can separate such three elements from the Earth, yet not completely...

### Johannis Isaaci Hollandi

...measure, but **Earth** must remain with it; otherwise, one could not create a **Body** <term>Corpus</term> <note>In alchemy, a *corpus* refers to the physical, tangible state of a substance, as opposed to its spirit or soul.</note> from it that would be tangible in its specific form. Therefore, the **Elements** are not separable, for the three elements—**Fire**, **Air**, and **Water**—carry up with them a subtle terrestrial portion from the coarse part of the **Earth**, through which they incorporate themselves so that they become dry and tangible, but not **fixed** <note>"Fixed" refers to a substance that can withstand high heat without evaporating or changing.</note>. For if one wishes to fix them, they must have something of the coarser part of the **Earth** within them; yet the Master must make these coarse parts of the Earth **subtle** <note>To "make subtle" (subtiliren) means to refine or break down a substance into its most pure, energetic, or powdered form.</note> before he joins them together, just as this shall be taught hereafter.

But the fact that the **Water** passes over with a yellow color comes from it being **distilled** from the fire, and the "burning" of the fire drives out a portion of the **Air** and **Fire** along with the **Water**, which causes the yellow hue. Then, they place it in the **Water-bath** <term>Balneum</term> <note>original: *Balneum*. ### Chapter 23.

Now we will resume our work: accordingly, when the jug, following the previous instructions, has stood in the <term>water bath</term> <note>original: "Balneo." A method of gentle, indirect heating where a vessel is placed in hot water, named for the "Bath of Mary" (Balneum Mariae).</note> in such a manner for two days and nights, take said jug out and let it stand for two or three days to settle. Then, separate it again through a filter and pour this liquid with the first portion and cover it.

This process of extracting, settling, and filtering must be repeated until the water no longer takes on any color, but remains pure and clear above the dregs; in this way, you have then obtained the **fire out of the earth**. Finally, remove the dregs mixed with the earth from the stone jug and place them into another vessel.

As an example, when wine comes from the winepress, it is filthy and cloudy, and casts out all filth, and settles **lees** and **dregs** <note>original: *Feces*; in an alchemical context, this refers to the solid impurities or sediment that settle out of a liquid.</note> at the bottom; it also separates from itself the <term>tartar</term> <note>original: *Tartarum*; the potassium bitartrate crystals that form on the inside of wine barrels.</note> onto the barrel, and these are nothing but bad dregs and harmful **humors** <note>original: *Humores*; here used to describe the "unbalanced" or waste fluids within the substance.</note> that depart above, below, and on all sides. ## Preface.

After this precious little book came into my hands during my search for the writings of famous persons, along with an accompanying written report stating that it came from Glaßberger, the former servant of the Polish nobleman Cortiski—who obtained it together with a mass <note>original: "una cum massa"</note> (by which I understand a certain portion of the tincture <note>original: "portione quadam tincturæ"</note>) from Mr. Johann Potroski, the servant of Mr. Michael Sendivogius—I did not want to withhold it from those who investigate the truth. Instead, I wished to promote its publication alongside the writings of Hollandus <note>Johann Isaac Hollandus and his son Isaac were celebrated for their practical, clear instructions in alchemy, contrasting with the often-obscure allegories of other authors.</note>, believing that these two leading figures of the Hermetic Art <note>The philosophical and magical tradition named after Hermes Trismegistus, often used as a synonym for alchemy.</note> are well-matched. One of them describes the rarest manual operations <term>Handgriffe</term> <note>Refers to the practical, physical techniques performed at the alchemical furnace.</note> that may be found in the whole of the chemical art, while the other has provided the clearest description of the secondary matter <note>original: "Materiæ secundæ" — In alchemical theory, the "first matter" is the raw essence of the universe, while the "secondary matter" is that essence already narrowed down into a specific substance (like a metal or mineral) ready for the Great Work.</note> or the seed of things <note>original: "spermatis rerum" — the generative life-force believed to exist within minerals and metals.</note>, described better than by all other philosophers. it is asserted in Sendivogius's *New Light* <note>original: *Sendivogii novo lumine*. This refers to his most famous work, *Novum Lumen Chymicum* (The New Chemical Light), published in 1604, which revolutionized alchemical theory by focusing on a "vital air."</note> that all metals <term>metalla</term> have their origin from a single prime matter <term>prima Materia</term> <note>The fundamental, formless substance from which all things were thought to be created.</note> or oily vapor of the elements <note>original: *vapore unctuoso Elementorum*</note>, after the Archeus <note>The *Archæus* was considered by alchemists like Paracelsus to be an internal, invisible "master craftsman" or vital force that directs the growth and formation of all living things and minerals.</note> has disposed the same vapor or central salt <term>Sal centrale</term> into the second matter <term>secundam Materiam</term> or metallic seed <term>sperma metallicum</term>. 

Thus, the foundation of metallic transformation <term>transmutatio</term> and improvement <term>melioratio metallicæ</term> <note>Alchemists used "improvement" to describe the process of refining "base" metals like lead into "noble" metals like gold.</note> is likewise based here upon this same oily vapor, and it is irrefutably proven (in which the entire host of philosophers agrees) that all the art and power of such transformation is nothing else, nor can be anything else, than that the lack of such fixed oiliness <term>Unctuosität</term> in the imperfect metals be replenished. 

This oiliness is found nowhere so abundantly as in common sulfur <term>Schwefel</term>, which in truth is nothing other than a pure and clear unctuosity, and as it were the fat of the earth, indeed of all nature. For what is all that is fatty in nature but Sulfur <term>Sulphur</term>, with which the lean water is tempered? And so it is also with metals: while they all have their body <term>Corpus</term> from Mercury <term>Mercurio</term> or quicksilver, the fact that they are ductile metals <note>original: *metalla ductibilia*. Metals that can be hammered or drawn out without breaking.</note> comes from Sulfur. If such sulfur were not there, they would likely have remained a running mercury <term>Mercurius currens</term> <note>Liquid quicksilver.</note>; for although the oiliness of sul- <note>The word is interrupted by the page break; the catchword indicates "Schwefel" (sulfur) continues on the next page.</note>

# Preface

[Sulfur] becomes clear, and one might well say of it that it dominates <term>dominates</term> <note>original: *dominiret*; from the Latin *dominari*, meaning to rule or master.</note> not only this entire world, but also Heaven and Hell. For what is the heavenly radiance other than **Sulfur**? What is all life other than warmth, which warmth must surely be fire and **Sulfur**? What is the fire of Hell other than **Sulfur**? What was the punishment of Sodom <note>original: *Sodomæ*; the biblical city destroyed by "fire and brimstone" (sulfur) in Genesis 19.</note> other than **Sulfur**? What is the physical blessing of God other than fatness, as the Psalmist says: *your footsteps drip with fatness*? <note>A reference to Psalm 65:11. In the chemical philosophy of the time, "fatness" or "unctuosity" was the defining characteristic of the element Sulfur.</note> Thus, **Sulfur** is, as it were, the most noble instrument through which God reveals both grace and punishment.

Therefore, it is not without reason that the basis of all transmutation <term>transmutation</term> <note>The alchemical transformation of one substance into another, typically base metals into gold or silver.</note> in this treatise is attributed to **Sulfur**. I still consider this treatise to be the work of Sendivogius <note>Michael Sendivogius (1566–1636), a renowned Polish alchemist and physician.</note>, until someone convinces me otherwise. I hold the opinion that he perhaps composed it in Polish or Latin, and it was afterwards translated into German by his aforementioned servant or someone else. Although one can perceive in Sendivogius’s writings that he read the German works <note>original: *Opera*.</note> of Paracelsus <note>Theophrastus Paracelsus (1493–1541), the influential Swiss-German physician and alchemist who wrote extensively in the vernacular.</note>, and would therefore have understood German himself, it is still not likely that he would have written anything in German himself. Be that as it may, it is an excellent treatise, which I hereby hand over to the reader, recommending him to God's protection and grace.

This is something the art-loving Artist should and must observe especially well if he wishes to escape the **labyrinth** <note>original: "Labyrintho"; a common metaphor for the confusing and contradictory nature of alchemical writings</note> and reach the correct path of the philosophers. ## On the Labyrinths of the Alchemists

<meta>The text begins mid-word, completing "Sulphur" from the previous page.</meta>

...**Sulphur** mixed within it; this is then combined with the rising water and gradually **coagulated** by the air at the surface <note>original: "am Tag"; a mining term referring to the light of day or the ground level</note>, being mingled with the coarse earth. However, that which is generated within the earth and in the ore called **ironstone** <note>original: "Eisenstein"; the primary ore from which iron is extracted</note> comes about through the mixture of **vitriolic salt** <term>vitriol; a sulfate salt that provides the metal's "sharp" or acidic quality</term> found in those same places in the earth. Because this vitriolic salt carries more sulfur within it than other salts do, it becomes hard within the earth and coagulates into ironstone. When this is processed through the **smelting furnace**, it reveals itself as iron, though it loses most of its sulfur in the process. Because the sulfur has escaped, the metal is thereafter more difficult to melt <note>original: "hartflüssiger"</note> than any other metal, for its remaining **Body** <term>Corpus; the physical, "salty" substance of a metal left after volatile elements are removed</term> consists only of sharp vitriolic salt and earth.

For this reason, iron also rusts so quickly in water or dampness; as the salt is gradually dissolved <note>original: "resolviret"</note>, the metal returns once again to earth. This is something the **lover of the art** <note>original: "Kunstliebende"; a respectful term for a dedicated practitioner of alchemy</note> will know and must observe with diligence: that all easily melted metals owe their easy flow solely to sulfur. Therefore, if one heats iron or steel until it glows and throws common combustible sulfur upon it, it will flow like lead. But because the sulfur is combustible and cannot remain there long, this fluid state cannot persist; rather, once the sulfur has burned away, the metal becomes unmeltable as before. This is presented to the lover of the art merely as a simple trial by way of illustration.

# Philosophical Treatise

The third group, who are highly learned and well-experienced in deception, despise the opinions of these two previous groups. They direct their path further toward philosophical **Transmutation**, in that they do not speak ill of metals and minerals, but rather praise them highly—provided they actually understood what they were seeking and knew what kind of substance and essence it truly was. According to all philosophical opinion, this substance is capable of bringing all imperfect metals, in great quantities, to perfection. However, because they neither understand nor recognize this substance, they do not know how to attain it, finding neither beginning, middle, nor end. 

Nevertheless, they intend to arrive at this art with all their might through their "wonderful" manual labor; indeed, using the most extraordinary vessels and glassware, earthen and metallic containers, and all manner of furnaces they construct for this purpose. They distill all kinds of <term>strong waters</term> <note>original: "starcke Wasser"; typically refers to corrosive mineral acids like nitric acid (aqua fortis) or hydrochloric acid used to dissolve metals</note>, in which they combine not just one, but often ten or twelve different mineral substances, such as salts, <term>Mercury</term> ☿ <note>original: "☿"; also known as quicksilver</note>, and the like. 

With these mixtures, they want to <term>dissolve</term> <note>original: "solviren"; the process of breaking down a solid into a liquid state</note> **Gold** ☉ and **Silver** ☽ <note>original: "☉" and "☽"; the sun and moon symbols used to represent the "perfect" noble metals</note> and other metals. Afterward, they seek to separate the <term>four elements</term> <note>The classic Greek elements: Earth, Water, Air, and Fire, believed to be the building blocks of all matter</note> and purify each one individually. Once these elements have been well-purified according to their methods, they reassemble them, <term>putrefy</term> <note>original: "putrificiren"; a stage in alchemy involving the "rotting" or breaking down of a substance, often associated with the color black</note> them, distill them, and finally <term>coagulate</term> <note>original: "coaguliren"; the process of thickening or solidifying a liquid into a solid mass</note> them into the right, true <term>Philosophers' Stone</term> <note>original: "Lap. Phil." or "Lapis Philosophorum"; the legendary goal of alchemy</note>.
