# Philosophical Treatise

...report a simple test (behind which, however, more is hidden than many might think) regarding common burning sulfur. Namely, when it is thrown into the fire upon the metals, it quickly enters into all metals (with the exception of gold) and mixes with them so that it is not easily separated from them. Silver, copper <note>original: ♀ (Venus)</note>, and iron <note>original: ♂ (Mars)</note> become very easily liquid because of it; tin <note>original: ♃ (Jupiter)</note> and lead become more difficult to melt than before; mercury is <term>coagulated</term> <note>turned from a liquid to a solid state</note> by it and becomes a beautiful red cinnabar <note>Mercury sulfide, often used as a pigment</note>, but all of this is unstable and combustible. 

The reason why burning sulfur so willingly unites and mixes with the metals is this: the six <term>imperfect metals</term> <note>Silver, copper, iron, tin, lead, and mercury—distinguished from gold, the "perfect" metal.</note> lack only an incombustible sulfur for their perfection. Therefore, they eagerly draw the combustible sulfur to themselves, as it is the very thing they lack. Gold, however, has no lack of sulfur, but is itself a sulfur matured and well-ripened <note>original: "ausgekochter," literally "boiled out," referring to the alchemical idea that nature "cooks" metals in the earth over time.</note> by nature. For this reason, it does not allow itself to be mixed with burning sulfur in the same way as the other metals. 

Furthermore, the lover of the Art <note>A common term for a practicing alchemist.</note> should also note here that no mineral salt <note>original: 🜔</note>—nor any vegetable or animal salt, no matter how skillfully it is extracted, purified, and prepared—will mix or unite with the perfect or imperfect metals, neither in flux nor otherwise. Instead, it always flows on top in the fire. The reason for this is that the metals are already [saturated] with superfluous salt...

Once you have this, you must take care that no sulfur or other great heat comes near it. If the lover of the Art then wishes to proceed with the operation and obtain the **metallic seed** from it, he must break it into small pieces like beans, then seal it tightly in a glass, and set it to digest <note>In alchemy, "digestion" refers to the application of gentle, continuous heat to a substance over a long period, mimicking the warmth of the womb or the earth.</note> for 14 days in a damp heat, or in warm sand. Then he will see a moisture emanate from it and cling everywhere to the glass, which will be very clear and bright, like dew from heaven. Then he must take the glass with its material and lute <note>To seal the joints of the apparatus with a specialized paste or clay to make it airtight.</note> a helm <note>The top part of a still, also known as an alembic head.</note> tightly upon it, and distill it through the sand—first gently, then strongly—and he will find in the receiver a wonderfully bright, clear, transparent, and heavy water. This he must pour for the third time over the dregs <note>original Latin: feces; the solid residue remaining after distillation.</note>, and distill it from them again; thus, the longer it takes, the more beautiful and heavy it becomes. He must then digest the same again in a fresh, tightly closed glass for 8 days in damp heat; afterwards, using a very gentle water bath <note>original Latin: Balneo; refers to the Balneum Mariae, or Mary’s bath, which provides even, gentle heating.</note>, draw off some of the **phlegm** <note>The tasteless, watery, and chemically inactive part of a substance that rises first during distillation.</note> from it; thus he will have at the bottom <note>original Latin: in fundo</note> the most beautiful, clearest sky-blue water, heavy in weight, which is the <term>first matter of metals</term> <note>original Latin: prima materia metallorum; the primordial, undifferentiated substance from which all metals were thought to grow.</note>. With this, the lover of the Art must proceed as mentioned in the Mineral Chapter; then, according to God’s will and blessing, he will achieve and obtain that which so many thousands have sought. For this, we wish him luck, blessing, salvation, and all prosperity from God the Almighty, Amen.

# Preface.

Even assuming that Basil and **Hollandus** wrote twenty years earlier than Paracelsus, it is not to be presumed that their writings were published immediately, such that Paracelsus could have transcribed them and studded his own writings with their work.

It can be proven from very ancient books that the supposed third principle—that of the **alkaline ash-salt** <term>alkaline ash-salt: *alcalischen Aschen-Salz*; the salt (such as potash) extracted from the ashes of burnt organic matter, representing the "Salt" principle in alchemy.</term> which resists fire in all things—has been known and used by **chemists** <note>original: "Chymicis."</note> for time immemorial. This is true even if the academic **schools** <note>Referring to traditional Scholastic or Galenic university education.</note> did not "frame it among the pillars" of the fundamental principles, as they now borrow from the books of our **guild** <note>original: "Zunfft"; the community of alchemists and practitioners of the "chemical art."</note> to teach today. ## Chapter I.

My child, the philosophers have followed nature and previously brought all things into water, without any **dregs** <term>Dregs: original: "Feces." In alchemy, this refers to the solid impurities or sediment remaining after a substance is purified or dissolved.</term>, before they made use of them in the **chemical art** <note>original: "chymischer Kunst"</note>. Likewise, the philosophers also sought the earth in the water, just as **God** the Almighty first placed the earth into the water, and they found the earth in the water, which they then called their **precious and dear stone** <note>A reference to the Philosopher's Stone, the ultimate goal of alchemy.</note>, since the earth is a beginning of all things. Therefore, one must take his earth and prepare it and make it fertile before one sows into it; for without preparation it cannot bear fruit because it is in itself **cold and dry** <note>In the Aristotelian system used by alchemists, Earth is defined by the qualities of coldness and dryness.</note>. If it is not moistened by the rain and warmed by the sun, it can bring forth no fruit; conversely, if it is scorched by the sun, it is also unfruitful. Therefore, it must be **tempered** <note>original: "temperirt." Meaning balanced or brought to a proper middle state.</note>, not too hot, nor too cold, nor too dry, nor too moist. To this end, the masters have invented a **strong water** <term>Strong water: original: "Aquafort" (from the Latin aqua fortis). A powerful solvent, often nitric acid, used by alchemists to dissolve metals and minerals.</term>, with which they might make the earth hot and moist; therein they have **dissolved** <term>Dissolved: original: "solviret." To break a solid substance down into a liquid state, a fundamental step in the alchemical process.</term> their earth, pouring on no more strong water than

<summary>This chapter introduces the fundamental alchemical principle of imitating the biblical Creation by finding "earth" within "water." It explains that the alchemical earth must be properly prepared and balanced in its qualities—neither too dry nor too wet—using a "strong water" solvent before it can be used to produce the Philosopher's Stone.</summary>

...she needs; for the philosophers write in a veiled manner <note>original: "verdeckter Weise"</note> thus: If our Stone is too dry, it brings forth no fruit; if it is too moist, it drowns the fruit; if it is too hot, it vanishes <note>original: "versleucht," meaning to evaporate or escape as vapor.</note>. Therefore, the Earth or the Stone must have no more Strong Water than is required for it alone to be dissolved <note>original: "solviret"</note>. But if you give the Earth too little Strong Water so that it is not dissolved, it will be much too dry and will be unable to bear fruit. In this matter, there is no specific weight to prescribe; weight in all things is nothing other than giving a thing its necessity, and neither more nor less.

From this, the wise men understood that one draws the Earth out of the water.

## Chapter IV.

This aforementioned process is the first **ordinance of the philosophers** <note>A standard procedure or rule established by the great alchemical authorities.</note>, and is an **augmentation** <term>Augmentation: original: "Vermehrung." The process of increasing the power, quality, or quantity of the alchemical material.</term> of the body. If you now wish to make an **increase** <term>Increase: original: "Augment."</term> of this white or red **calx** <term>Calx: original: "Kalcks." A powdery metallic oxide produced by heating a metal in air.</term>, put it into such a glass, No. 1, and place it in a furnace and turn the vessel over and over again in order to **fix** <term>Fix: original: "figiren." ## Chapter XXVII.

Therefore, cement well, at least 7 times, if you wish to have perfection.

## Cap. XXVIII. <insert>28</insert>
### Sublimation of Mercury to the Red.

Mercury is sublimated to the Red in the following manner: Take <term>strong-water <note>original: "Starckwasser"; a corrosive mineral acid, typically nitric acid</note></term> made from Roman <term>vitriol <note>original symbol: ♁; metal sulfates used to create acids</note></term>, rock alum, <term>plume alum <note>original: "alumine plumoso"; likely a fibrous variety of alum or asbestos</note></term>, and <term>sal-ammoniac <note>original: "Salmiac"; ammonium chloride</note></term>. ### Sublimation of Mercury to the White.

<margin>Take:</margin> <term>Strong Water <note>original: "Starck Wasser"; likely referring to Aqua Fortis or a similar acidic solvent</note></term>, made from <term>calamine <note>original: "Galmey"; a zinc-bearing ore</note></term> and <term>eggshell lime <note>original: "Eyerkalck"; calcium oxide produced by burning eggshells</note></term>, 1 pound of each; rock alum and white <term>vitriol <note>original: "Vitriol"; a sulfate mineral, here specifically zinc sulfate</note></term>, 2 pounds each; arsenic, 1 pound; saltpeter, 5 pounds. # Johannes Isaacus Hollandus.

<margin>NB: To finish.</margin>
...finish. My child should know that in our Work there are seven orders <note>Stages or sequential processes</note> that one must perform in their entirety before the Work reaches perfection. The first is <term>cementation <note>original: "cementiren"; the process of heating a solid metal with powdered reagents to refine it</note></term>, the second is <term>solution <note>original: "solviren"; dissolving a solid into liquid form</note></term>, the third is <term>feeding <note>original: "speisen"; the addition of "mercurial water" or other substances to the matter to nourish its growth</note></term>, the fourth is <term>putrefaction <note>original: "putreficiren"; the breaking down of matter through slow, moist heat, often signaled by the substance turning black</note></term>, the fifth is <term>coagulation <note>original: "coaguliren"; thickening or solidifying a liquid</note></term>, the sixth is <term>digestion <note>original: "digeriren"; prolonged heating at a constant temperature to mature the substance</note></term>, the seventh is <term>fixation <note>original: "figiren"; making a volatile substance stable so it no longer evaporates or changes when exposed to fire</note></term>.

<margin>Note here</margin>
Know also that all these operations for the white and the red <note>The "White Stone" for silver-making and the "Red Stone" for gold-making</note> are to be handled in exactly the same way, except for the seventh, which is <term>fixation</term>; for the red, it must stand much longer in the fire than for the white. Furthermore, the red requires more heat during fixation than the white, because the red must be made to resemble the nature of a man, while the white follows the nature of a woman. Therefore, the red must stand longer and hotter than the white until it transforms into a beautiful color resembling gold, by which one recognizes that it is perfect.

<margin>D <unclear>Salt</unclear></margin>
Know further, my child, that through <term>cementation</term>, the White Stone changes from being cold and moist to being hot and dry. However, in <term>solution</term> it becomes moist again; in <term>putrefaction</term> it becomes subtle; and in <term>digestion</term> it becomes dry, coarse, earthy, and fixed again. Furthermore, my child, know that when the Medicine comes out of <term>putrefaction</term> and out of <term>digestion</term>, it is congealed, yet one cannot yet perform <term>projection <note>The final act of casting a small amount of the Philosopher's Stone onto a base metal to transform it into silver or gold</note></term> with it. This is because it is far too subtle, and even if you were to attempt <term>projection</term> with it, it would not [last] in the fire.

<margin>Volatile <note>original: "Volat"</note></margin>

For if no <term>Body <note>original: "Corpus"; the physical substance or metallic base that gives the medicine a form to inhabit</note></term> were added to the <term>Medicine <note>The highly refined alchemical substance capable of transmuting metals</note></term>, one would be unable to perform a perfect <term>projection <note>original: "Projection"; the final stage of alchemy where the Medicine is cast upon base metals to transform them into silver or gold</note></term>, even if the Medicine were applied. For although it is now truly Medicine, it is nonetheless not a Body, and because of its fineness it will not take hold upon an imperfect body <note>Such as lead or tin</note>, as those are too earthy and coarse. Indeed, even if you threw it upon the finest silver, it would show no effect, because they are alienated and distinct from each other due to the Medicine's great fineness.

Therefore, let us now add the fourth element to the Medicine: Take your Medicine out of the <term>digestion <note>original: "Digestion"; the process of maturing a substance through gentle, continuous heat</note></term>, and divide it into three parts of equal weight. Rub them on a clean stone. Take as much <term>silver-calx <note>original: "Silberkalck"; silver that has been reduced to a fine, white powder through chemical processing</note></term>—which I will teach you to prepare here—as one third of your Medicine weighs. Thus you have four parts: namely, 3 parts Medicine and one part silver-calx. Mix these well together.

<margin>Note well:</margin> In such a manner, some have **calcined** <note>reduced to powder through intense heat</note> the **bodies** <note>original: Corpora; the solid metallic or mineral components</note> and dissolved the **spirits** <note>the volatile, active essences of a substance</note>, subsequently **imbibing** <note>original: imbibiret; soaking or saturating</note> the bodies with the spirits. ## Chapter XLVIII. <insert>48</insert>

### The Seventh Work.

Some have taken liquid mercury <note>original symbol: ☿; also known as quicksilver</note> and washed it with salt and vinegar until it stood as bright as a mirror; then they took rock alum <note>original: Alumen roche; a naturally occurring potassium alum</note> and evaporated it over a small fire, while retaining its spirits, until it was so dry that it turned to dust. Of this alum they took 3 pounds; calamine stone <note>original: Lapis Calaminaris; a zinc ore</note>, eggshell lime <note>original: Calx ovorum</note>, and salt, 1 pound each; and 3 pounds of washed mercury. They ground these together upon a stone and sublimated <note>a process of heating a substance until it vaporizes and then collecting the solid deposit</note> them, first with a small fire and subsequently with a more violent one. 

They repeated this sublimation seven times so that they might soak the mercury with the white spirits of the alum, for rock alum is full of white spirits, just as Roman alum is full of red spirits. For people make copper <note>original symbol: ♀</note> white with calamine stone without any other addition—indeed, as white as silver. Furthermore, one allows eggshell lime to dissolve in distilled vinegar, and the calces <note>the powdery metallic residue left after heating</note> of copper are often soaked with the dissolved eggshells; then, when these calces are reduced back into a solid body, it is as white as silver. This is well known to those who can perform whitenings <note>original: Albationes; chemical procedures used to give base metals a silver-like appearance</note> in order to deceive people.

### Chapter LIII. <insert>53</insert>
### The Eleventh Work.

The Quinta Essentia will remain at the bottom of the **distilling vessel** <note>original: "Destillatorio"</note>. Afterwards, take that which had risen during **sublimation** <note>referring to the solid matter that vaporized and reformed at the top of the flask in the previous step</note>, and do the same with it: extract its Quinta Essentia. Take it then and let it **putrefy** <term>A process of slow digestion or fermentation in a warm environment, often using organic heat</term> in horse manure or a water bath until it dissolves into oil; then it will be as sweet as honey.

This oil has unspeakably great virtues for driving away all kinds of plagues and keeping a person healthy; it heals all kinds of wounds, both external and internal, as well as leprosy, **etc.** <term>2c.</term> <gloss>Gloss: I mean that one must combine the Quinta Essentia and the sublimated matter into one oil and use it as taught above.</gloss>

## Chapter LXV <insert>65</insert>

Now we wish to discuss **Solution** <term>The process of dissolving a solid into a liquid state</term>: After the **mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note> has been sublimated, dissolve it first in the **Water of the Philosophers** <note>original: *aqua Philosophorum*; a specialized alchemical solvent, often a strong acid or "mercurial water"</note>. Place the mercury thus dissolved into the sublimation pot, set the **alembic head** <note>original: *Helm*; the cooling cap of a distilling apparatus</note> upon it, and attach a **receiver** <note>original: *Vorlage*; the vessel that collects the distillate</note> to it. Seal everything tightly with **lute** <note>original: *lutiret*; a clay or paste used to make the joints of the apparatus airtight</note> and distill at first with a gentle fire until all the watery moisture has come over, and you see the mercury begin to sublime into the head. Then strengthen the fire slightly so that it sublimes nicely for 6 hours; at the end of these 6 hours, make the bottom of the pot glow modestly, and for the fourth 6-hour period <note>The author implies four stages of six hours each, totaling a full day</note>, let the pot stand in the heat; this makes 24 hours in total. 

When your water has been drawn off, let it cool and remove the alembic head and take out the **mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note>. The water that remains in the receiver is no longer useful, though one might keep it for the **Calcination** <term>The process of heating a substance to high temperatures to reduce it to a powder</term> of certain bodies; otherwise, it is of no use. This is because the **living silver** <note>original: *Argentum vivum*; mercury</note> has carried away all the power and the whole **Tincture** <term>The elusive essence or "soul" of a substance that carries its medicinal or transformative power</term> with it, because they are of the same kind. From a horse comes a horse, from a dog a dog, etc. All tinctures that are in the water are like the **mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note> and have collectively received their initial nature and first origin in the **ores** <term>original: *Mineren*</term> from the mercury, for he is the father of them all. Thus, he <note>the mercury</note> carries all the tinctures away with him into his own nature from then on, and weds them for the first time in the Solution; for all natures have become water—

<margin>#</margin> [become], and, if the **mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note> is simultaneously turned into water, then they become one together and are united in the **Solution** <term>The chemical process of dissolving a solid into a liquid state</term>. Thus, a marriage is formed between the **Tincture** <note>The active alchemical principle capable of transforming and coloring metals</note> and the **mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note>, which marriage hereafter in the **Fixation** <term>The process by which a volatile substance is made stable and resistant to heat</term> shall be regarded as the matrimonial work. Therefore **Aristotle** <note>The Greek philosopher was often cited in alchemical texts as a foundational authority on the nature of matter</note> says: I do not believe that one can transfer any thing from its own nature into another, unless one first brings that same thing into its primary nature; only then is it possible to bring and transfer it into another nature. All things were water in the beginning; therefore, whoever wishes to attain any perfection, or make an **Elixir** or the **Philosopher's Stone** <note>original Latin: *lapidem Philosophorum*</note>, must necessarily first turn everything together into water.

### Chapter LXVII. <insert>67</insert>

When it has thus been dissolved and sublimated, then sublimate the **mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note> 3, 4, or 5 times, until it leaves behind no **dregs** <note>original: *Feces*; the solid impurities left after distillation or sublimation</note>, for that is what **Morienus** <note>Morienus Romanus, a legendary alchemist known for his dialogue with King Khalid, symbolizing the transition from the black stage to the white stage of the work</note> says: "Unless you de-blacken it and make it clear, like a crystal, you have accomplished nothing in the **Mastery**" <term>The Great Work or *Magnum Opus* of alchemy</term>. Sublimate it, therefore, as many times until the bottom of the pot remains as beautiful as it was when you first put the matter into it, and it is as clear as a crystal. Then it is prepared up to the point of **calcination** <term>The process of heating a substance to high temperatures in order to reduce it to a fine powder or ash</term>, in order to be calcined. Therefore, a **philosopher** <note>original: *Philosophus*</note> says: "Christ is taken from the cross and laid in the grave." <note>This religious metaphor compares the chemical state—where the purified matter sits immobile in the vessel—to the Passion and burial of Christ, preceding a "resurrection" into a higher form.</note>

## Chapter LXXVI. <insert>76</insert>

### The Twentieth Work.

# Mineral Work

[The author] says: "Whoever cannot make silver from gold, can also not make gold from silver." In this way, it will congeal into the <term>Philosophers' Stone <note>original: *Stein der Philosophen*</note></term>. Break open the glass, and you will have a snow-white stone, as clear as a crystal and as meltable as wax. This stone may be pulverized, and it transforms tin and <term>mercury <note>original symbol: ☿</note></term>—and indeed, even <term>gold <note>original symbol: ☉; literally "the Sun," the alchemical correspondence for gold.</note></term>—into true silver, of better quality than that which comes from the mines. 

You can multiply this stone at any time with sublimated mercury; specifically, seven parts of the sublimate to one part of the stone. # Chapter 77
## The Shape of the Fixing-Glass.
### No. 24.

My child should know that this is the fixing-glass <note>A vessel designed to "fix" volatile substances, making them stable under heat so they do not evaporate away.</note> in which all things are fixed. It should be made of thick glass, and its round head must be curved inward at the top, just as the belly of a drinking glass is curved inward at the top, with a sharp, long point hanging downwards. From this point, the drops that steam up from below as vapors may fall back down again <note>This describes a "reflux" mechanism, where evaporated liquids condense on the upper point and drip back into the bottom of the flask, ensuring nothing is lost.</note>. On the side, there should be a tube through which to pour the material and allow the <term>calx <note>original: *Kalck*; a powder produced by heating a metal or mineral to its breaking point.</note></term> to fall in, and then to pour the water over it. Upon this tube, a small round piece of glass should be ground to fit and close tightly. 

Then, grind glass powder with linseed oil so finely that one could paint with it. Brush a little of this with a paintbrush onto the rim of the tube, and then place the small round glass upon it, and on top of that, a lead weight. When it is dry, it will be as firm as if it were glass itself, and no spirits <note>Vapors or volatile gases.</note> may penetrate through it. You can then brush the vessel once more all the way around with the brush and let it dry well; thus, you will find no fault in your <term>lute <note>original: *Luto*; a specialized alchemical cement or paste used to seal vessels airtight.</note></term>. However, you will have difficulty getting it open again; you must do that with a razor, for this powder—

My child should know that this matter is by nature <term>styptic <note>original: *stiptisch*; meaning astringent or contracting. Take this prepared <term>Vitriol <note>original: *Vitriol*; here referring to the sulfate mineral after its initial purification and reddening mentioned on the previous page.</note></term> and put it into a glass <term>ampulla <note>A flask or bottle with a rounded body.</note></term> or "egg." ### Chapter LXXXVI. <gloss>86</gloss>

## The 24th Work from Arsenic.

Now, my child, I will teach you to make the white Stone from <term>Arsenic</term> <note>Symbol: ⚦; in alchemy, this usually refers to "white arsenic" or arsenic trioxide.</note>: Take 4 or 5 lbs. of Arsenic, crush it into a fine powder, then take <term>Alum</term>, <term>Eggshell Lime</term> <note>original: *Eyerkalck*; calcium oxide made by calcining eggshells.</note>, <term>Calamine</term> <note>original: *Galmenstein*; a zinc ore.</note>, and common Salt, all dried over a gentle fire—namely 2 parts of common salt to 1 part of each of the others—rub them together, and for every 4 lbs. of Arsenic, take a total of 8 lbs. of the other materials. Mix them together, place them in a <term>sublimation vessel</term> <note>A specialized container for heating solids into vapor to purify them.</note>, and <term>sublimate</term> the Arsenic. That which has been <term>sublimated</term> <note>The purified solid that collects at the top of the vessel.</note>, rub back into the <term>residue</term> <note>original: *Feces*; the waste material left at the bottom.</note>, and sublimate it once more. ## Chapter LXXXIX. 89

When the 18 weeks have now passed, take out your matter and take as much weight of it as you wish; grind it to a powder and place it into the <term>fixing-glass</term> <note>original: *Figir-Glas*; a glass vessel used in the process of "fixation," where a volatile substance is made stable under heat.</note>. Pour upon it our red <term>burning water</term> <note>original: *brennenden Wasser*; likely a reference to a strong solvent or *aqua ardens*.</note>, of the same weight as the powder, and seal it or plug it very tightly. Let it <term>dissolve</term> <note>original: *solviren*</note> and become clear, then take it out and pour it into a distillation pot with an <term>alembic</term> <note>original: *Alembico*; the "head" or cap of a still used to collect and direct vapors.</note> on top. Distill it via a <term>water bath</term> <note>original: *Balneum*</note> in lukewarm heat, and the <term>receiver</term> <note>original: *Recipient*; the vessel that catches the condensed liquid.</note> should be very well <term>luted</term> <note>original: *lutiret*; sealed with a paste called "lute" to prevent vapors from escaping.</note>. You must have an alembic that has a tube at the top, for you must distill it 6 times, and each time pour on fresh red water; your matter will remain in the glass like thick honey. Then take it out of the water bath and place it on the furnace in sifted ashes. Give it gentle fire at first, and henceforth <term>gradually</term> <note>original: *gradatim*</note> increase it; first, the "air" will pass over as water. Then one should provide another receiver, and it will pass over as a <term>Gold-Oil</term>, so that the <term>helm</term> <note>original: *Helm*; the top part of the still.</note> and the receiver will shine like gold. Foreword to the Treatise on the Cabala of Hollandus

## Foreword to the Treatise
# CABALA OF HOLLANDUS.

Beloved reader, no more of the following treatise has come into my hands than what I quite gladly share with you here; should I receive the rest as well, it shall, God willing, likewise not be withheld from you by me. Without doubt, Hollandus <note>Johann Isaac Hollandus, a celebrated Dutch alchemist whose identity remains mysterious, though his works were highly influential in the 17th and 18th centuries.</note> executed this treatise excellently; if only one had it all together as he himself arranged it, because this is a subject of highly important content and great emphasis. And the most excellent men frequently refer in their writings to the art of the Cabala <note>original: *Cabalam*; referring to Kabbalah, a Jewish mystical tradition that Christian alchemists adapted to explain the secrets of nature and divinity.</note>, which signifies an art that from antiquity and its first beginning has been entrusted to its disciples through oral tradition by the enlightened and wise. This is now described as consisting of two parts, one of which is called of *Bereshit* <note>original: *de Bresith*; referring to the "Work of Creation" (Ma’aseh Bereshit) based on the first chapters of Genesis.</note> and Cosmology, which is to say, through which the powers of created natural and heavenly things are explained, and the mysteries of the Divine Law and Holy Scripture are elucidated with philosophical reasons; thus, this part is, as it were, entitled to the name of Natural Magic <note>original: *Magiæ Naturalis*; at this time, "magic" referred to the study of the hidden properties of the natural world.</note>. The other is named of the *Chariot* <note>original: *de Marcana*; likely a corruption of *Ma'aseh Merkabah*, the "Work of the Chariot," focusing on the divine realm and celestial hierarchies.</note>, which is, so to speak, a concurrent Theology, dealing with the profoundly deep Divine and Angelic <note>original: *Englischen*; here meaning "of the angels" (*Engel*), not the English nation.</note> powers and the contemplation of holy names and designations, wherein the letters, numbers, figures, things, and names—likewise the essence of the elements, the lines, points, and accents—are all interpreted with deep contemplativeness and the significance of great mysteries. Herewith
->fare thee well.<-

# C A B A L A

#### Chapter I.

My child, in order first and above all to write about the planet Jupiter <note>In the symbolic language of alchemy, the planet Jupiter represents the metal Tin.</note> in a metallic way, it is first necessary to know and be acquainted with what kind of matter it is composed of, namely: from Sulfur, Mercury <note>original: ☿</note>, and Salt <note>original: 🜔. These three—Sulfur, Mercury, and Salt—are known as the *Tria Prima*, the three primary principles that alchemists believed made up all material substance.</note>. Thus, it is also not sufficient that one merely knows how all metals are created from Sulfur, Salt, and Mercury; rather, he must also be aware of how many different parts of these three first principles exist within each thing in particular. This is to be understood as follows: it has no more than one kind of Mercury, but many kinds of Salt, and also only one kind of Sulfur. On this point, it must be observed and perceived with particular diligence: namely, that at all times, of these two parts, there is no more than one kind of Sulfur and one kind of

## Chapter II.

BE it known to my child in the aforementioned manner, that the Salts are manifold, namely of Saturn <note>original: ♄, representing Lead</note>, Jupiter <note>original: ♃, representing Tin</note>, Mars <note>original: ♂, representing Iron</note>, the Sun <note>original: ☉, representing Gold</note>, Venus <note>original: ♀, representing Copper</note>, Mercury <note>original: ☿, representing Quicksilver</note>, and the Moon <note>original: ☽, representing Silver</note>. ### Chapter III.

Furthermore, I wish to make known to my child <note>Alchemical authors often addressed the reader as "my child" or "my son," indicating a master-apprentice relationship.</note> the reason why two planets are so similar to each other in form and properties—both in color and appearance, as well as in hardness and softness—in this way:

You see that Jupiter <note>original: ♃; the metal Tin.</note> and Saturn <note>original: ♄; the metal Lead.</note> are entirely and in everything equal to each other in form, and also in color, both before and after melting, as if they were the same metal. And why? Note first this reason: namely, because the <term>Salt of Jupiter</term> <note>original: Sal Jovis; the "salt" or crystalline essence extracted from tin.</note> was an alum, yet not an alum or salt from which the Salt of Saturn is taken. The reason is that Rock Alum <note>original: Allaun de Roche; a naturally occurring potassium alum.</note> is not like <term>Stone Flax</term> <note>original: Steinflachs; a term for fibrous minerals such as asbestos or "feather alum."</note> or *Alumen Plumosum* <note>original: Alumen Plumosum; "feathered alum," known for its fibrous, hair-like crystals.</note>. ## Concerning the Book of JOHN ISAAC HOLLANDUS, on the <term>Philosopher's Stone</term> <note>original Latin: Lapide Philosophorum; the ultimate goal of alchemy, a substance capable of transmuting base metals into gold and healing all illnesses</note>.

The cause is this: in the <term>vegetable work</term> <note>original Latin: vegetabili opere</note> there is much coagulating, dissolving, and <term>rectifying</term> <note>original Latin: rectificirens; the process of purifying a substance through repeated distillation</note>, preparing the <term>spirits</term> <note>volatile essences or vapors</note> well so that they do not fly away, and also making many kinds of <term>strong-waters</term> <note>original German: Starck-Wasser; usually refers to corrosive acids like nitric acid</note>, and <term>fixing</term> <note>original German: figiren; the process of making a volatile substance stable and resistant to heat</note> many watery spirits. This requires much careful management with many kinds of concerns, so as to guard oneself that the spirits do not break the vessels; for through their fatty moistures they often cause the glasses to shatter if one gives them too much and too strong a fire when they are nearly fixed, and then they rise up, and

<term>Projection</term> <note>the final stage of alchemy where the Stone is cast upon a base metal to transform it into gold or silver</note>; if you lose even a little of the <term>fire</term> <note>original symbol: △; heat is the primary driver of alchemical change, and its loss prevents the "ripening" of the substance</note>, then your medicine will not be deeply colored, and it will also lose its <term>entry</term> <note>the ability of the alchemical substance to penetrate and permeate the "pores" of a base metal</note>; if it has too much <term>Air</term> <note>original Latin: Aeris; representing the gaseous or volatile state</note>, it flies away; if it then has too much <term>Water</term> <note>original symbol: ▽; representing the liquid or cold state</note>, the <term>spirits</term> <note>volatile substances produced during distillation</note> are drowned so that one cannot <term>fix</term> <note>original: figiren; to turn a volatile or liquid substance into a solid that can withstand heat</note> them; if it then has too much Earth, it is too dry, so that it has no melting capacity nor any entry.

### On the Philosopher's Stone ###

...otherwise it would be against nature and all reason that one could make metal out of any such **seed** <note>original: *Sperma*</note>, blood, or eggs; where nothing exists, seek not to pull anything from the imperfect thing. To transmute metals into **gold** <note>original: ☉ (*Sol*)</note> and **silver** <note>original: ☾ (*Luna*)</note> from such things is contrary to reason and nature, and is impossible. ### Johann Isaac Hollandus

Those who undertake to make the **Philosophers’ Stone** <note>original: *Stein der Philosophorum*. The legendary substance capable of turning base metals into gold and granting long life.</note> and bring it, through good **regulation of the fire** <term>regulation of the fire</term> <note>original: *Regiment des Feuers*. And the ignorant do not understand this; for once they have made their stone and united it well, so that it displays its colors as it is meant to, it must afterwards be made subtle and volatile again, if it is to have or perform an **ingress** <term>ingress</term> <note>original: *Ingress*. # ->On the Philosophers’ Stone.<- <note>original: *De lapide Philosophico*</note>

I adjure you by the living **Son of God**, that you do not reveal the **secret** <term>secret</term> <note>original: *Secret*. In alchemy, this refers to the "Arcanum" or the hidden key to the transformation of matter.</note> to anyone but your own sons, provided it seems to you that he has the love of **God**, so that your soul, and mine as well, be not damned because of the great hardship that might come from it. Open your eyes and
<margin>588</margin> ears, see and hear the great holiness that is in nature: that one may complete and finish all **Philosophers’ Stones** <note>original: *Lapides Philosophicos*</note>, in whatever manner they are composed, in the **Great Work** <term>Great Work</term> <note>original: *grossen Werck*. The entire process of creating the Philosophers' Stone.</note> of which we speak here, both for the **White** and for the **Red** <note>The "White" (Albedo) is the stage producing the stone that transmutes metal to silver; the "Red" (Rubedo) is the final stage for transmuting metal into gold.</note>, in a single vessel and a single furnace.

Mark well what I tell you: if you take **Moon** <note>original: *☽* (the symbol for the Moon/Silver).</note> and **Mercury** <note>original: *Mercurium*</note> without the addition of **Sun** <note>original: *☉* (the symbol for the Sun/Gold).</note> together in this manner, you can soon make the **Stone** from them, both for the White and for the Red, in one vessel and one furnace. Now someone might ask: why then does one take **Sun** and **Moon** together into the Work? This is done because the **Sun** is **fixed** <term>fixed</term> <note>original: *fix*. A substance that is "fixed" can endure the heat of the fire without evaporating.</note>, and thus the work becomes all the shorter. If your **Moon** were fixed in the Work, then the Stone for the White would be made. ...they dissolved the Stone and solidified it again, doing this 20 or 30 times, hoping to make the Stone meltable so that it might have an **Ingress** <term>Ingress</term> <note>The "entry" or ability of the alchemical medicine to penetrate and transform a base metal.</note>; but they found nothing. And this is the **Solution of the Ancients**. Their solution is not achieved through the pouring on of rainwater, but with a **dry water** <note>original symbol: ▽; a paradoxical term for Mercury, which acts like a liquid but does not wet the hands</note>, which is **Mercury** <note>original: *Merc.*</note>, and this is the foundation of the art. Regarding this, **Rhasis** <note>A famous 9th-century Persian alchemist and physician</note> says: "Unless you dissolve the body, you otherwise labor in vain." **Geber** <note>The Latinized name of Jabir ibn Hayyan, often called the "Father of Chemistry"</note> says of this solution in the *Book of Truth* within the *Turba* <note>The *Turba Philosophorum* or "Assembly of the Philosophers," one of the oldest and most influential alchemical texts</note>: "The surest way in the art is **Reduction**—that is, that one dissolves the bodies into a clear, beautiful water from which they were originally generated." In this water, **Spirit, Soul, and Body** <note>original: *Spir. Anima & Corpus*; the three components alchemists believed made up all matter</note> are preserved.

Geber says further: when they had converted the bodies into **Mercury**, so that they might pass through a cloth, they then said, "Now we have an **element of fire**."

He says further that from the coarseness of the water, the **Earth** would be made, and they said, "We also have the other elements, such as **Fire** <note>original symbol: △</note> and **Salt** <note>original symbol: 🜔</note>."

# On the Philosophers' Stone

The third stage is **Purification** <note>original: *Säuberung*; the process of removing impurities from the alchemical matter</note>, of which purification **Morienus** <note>A legendary 7th-century alchemist said to have taught the secrets of the Stone to the Umayyad prince Khalid ibn Yazid</note> says: the earth is putrefied with the water and is made pure, and then, through God’s help, the entire **mastery** <note>original: *Meisterschafft*; the completed alchemical process</note> is achieved.

And the **Philosophical Assembly** <note>original: *Turba Philosophica*; referring to the *Turba Philosophorum*, one of the oldest Latin alchemical texts</note> says: moisten the dry with the wet, for the dry is the Earth, and the wet is the **Water** <term>🜄; the alchemical symbol for the element of Water</term>; see, now we have purified the Water and the **Earth** <term>🜔; likely a symbol for Salt or Earth, representing the fixed, solid component</term>.

<margin>My 3</margin>
The fourth stage is the **evaporation of water** <note>original: *evaporatio aquæ*</note>, as the **Water of Paradise** <note>original: *🜄 paradisi*; a poetic term for the highly distilled, pure solvent used in the Work</note> rises into the heavens and falls back down to the earth in drops; they call this **making it like the Sun** <note>original: *☉n*; using the symbol for the Sun/Gold as a verb, meaning to solarize or transmute toward gold</note>, and through this rising and falling it becomes a powder that before was only **kneaded** <note>original: *impastiret*</note> into the Earth. This rising they called "Air," so you have **Water** <term>🜄</term>, Air, and **Earth** <term>🜔</term>. This is what the philosophers mean when they say: when it has been made white, pour the Water of Paradise over it and let it **sublimate** <term>Sublimation; the process where a solid turns into vapor and then back to solid, used here to purify the spirit</term> until it becomes a spirit called the **Bird of Hermes** <note>original: *Hermes=Vogel*; a famous alchemical symbol representing the volatile spirit that must be "winged" (vaporized) and then "grounded" (fixed)</note>.

Of this, Morienus says: in the end, there remains for you a **calcined** <note>reduced to ash by heat</note> earth, sand, and ashes. And **Hermes** and **Geber** <note>Jabir ibn Hayyan, an influential 8th-century polymath and "father" of Islamic alchemy</note> say: do not despise the ashes, for you shall find at the bottom a glowing ash, and you shall find within it a precious **adamant** <note>A legendary stone of indestructible hardness, here referring to the crystalline form of the Philosophers' Stone</note>. Afterward they say: add to it the **Ferment** <term>ℵ; the symbol Aleph, used here to represent the "yeast" or catalyst that triggers the final transformation</term>, so that they can turn it into a white powder. Then it must be drenched with the Water of Paradise, in which fine **gold** <note>original: *Aur.*, abbreviation for *Aurum*</note> should be **amalgamated** <note>blended into a liquid or paste-like state</note>; and this drenching they call **fermenting**.

The soul cleanses the imperfect **Body**, for it brings the **Ferment** <term>Fermentum; an agent of transformation, like yeast, that "leavens" the base matter into gold</term> to its true nature. Therefore they provide a **Ferment** when the **Gold** <term>Aurum; the pure solar metal</term> is mixed with the **Paradise Water** <note>original: *Paradieß-Wasser*; a poetic name for a highly refined, universal solvent</note>.

This is what **Morienus** <note>A legendary hermit-alchemist often cited as a primary authority on the union of spirit and matter</note> says: "Unless you perfectly cleanse and whiten the powders, and afterward pour the soul into them and unite them with one another, you have done and achieved nothing toward our mastery." For this reason, the Philosopher **Bautin** <note>likely a reference to an authority cited in the *Turba Philosophorum*</note> says: "Gather the soul with the purified **Body** <term>Corpore</term> and **Spirit** <term>Spiritu</term>; then its spirit will be added to it, and they shall rejoice with one another, for they are transformed from a single nature and coarse things, and have now become subtle." 

And this is what the Philosophers say in the **Book of Truth** <note>original: *codice veritatis*</note>: "The **Spirits** <term>Spiritus; the volatile, gaseous elements</term> are not gathered with the **Body** <term>Corpore</term> until they have been perfectly freed from all their impurity." In this **Conjunction** <term>The "chemical wedding" or union of the fixed and volatile aspects of the Stone</term> there are wondrous things, for all the colors of the whole world, as many as can be imagined, are enclosed within it, and in the end they all become a single color, which is red. # Johann Isaac Hollandus.

But the reason the Ancients wrote about such things with such obscure words was for the sake of the unwise, who are not **sons of the art** <note>original: "filii artis"; a traditional term for initiated alchemists</note>, so that they should not understand it; for it is meant to remain hidden.

Therefore, they also established many chapters so that the unlearned might think our art is very difficult. In each chapter, they mentioned many foreign things and gave them many foreign names, such as **Reduction**, **Solution**, **Ablution** <note>cleansing or washing of a substance</note>, **Sublimation**, **Distillation**, **Coagulation**, **Calcination**, **Fixation**, and other **diverse names** <note>original: "diversa nomina"</note> and manual operations, as I have said before.

## Now observe how the Ancients found such names in the Work.

And if you wish to perform a Work just as the Ancients, our ancestors, performed it themselves, then take **Mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note> which comes from the interior of the earth where one mines **Gold** <note>original symbol: ☉</note> or **Silver** <note>original symbol: ☾</note>, and not the quicksilver that is made through art <note>likely referring to mercury refined from cinnabar rather than found in its native metallic state near precious metals</note>. Melt it in a crucible with **Borax** <term>a flux used in metallurgy to lower the melting point and remove impurities</term>, and you will find what metal is within it: if it is an imperfect metal <note>such as lead or tin</note>, then the **Mercury** is of no use for our Work; but if you find **Gold** and **Silver**, then it is good; and if you find no **Body** at all, it is also good.

Of such **Mercury**, take as much as you wish,

When the **Mercury** <term>☿</term> fell down again, it would no longer mix with the body <note>the solid physical residue</note> and slowly became earth. ...[tra]pped, filth, dung; and they were deceived, for they are not our children <note>A traditional alchemical phrase referring to the "Sons of Art" or true initiates; those who are not "children" are the uninitiated who fail to understand the allegories</note>.

Therefore **Morienus** <note>Morienus Romanus, a legendary 7th-century alchemist</note> says: **Sources** <note>original: *Origines*</note>—wash, cleanse <note>original: *mundificirt*</note>, and purify the **Laton** <term>Laton; an impure metallic substance, often likened to brass or copper, representing the matter before it reaches solar purity</term> with the water, so that a **Union** <term>Conjunctio; the chemical and spiritual marriage of the principles of the Work</term> may occur between the **Body, Soul, and Spirit** <note>original: *Corpore Anima & Spiritu*</note>. 

And the foolish think that one should wash the **Body** <note>original: *Corpus*; the solid matter</note> with common water: for this reason they **calcined** <term>calcinirt; reduced a substance to a fine powder through intense heat</term> it with salt, rubbed it on a stone, and washed it with clear water; and they did this for so long that the water ran off beautifully clear, yet they were just as close to the Work as when they began, and they lost their money, effort, and labor.

**Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the mythical founder of alchemy</note> and **Geber** <note>Jabir ibn Hayyan, a central figure in early Islamic alchemy</note> say: know that our art is nothing other than a drawing of water out of the earth and pouring it back over it again, until it is perfected <note>original: *perficirt*</note>, washed, and cleansed with the earth. The ignorant do not understand this and remain in their fantasies; they did not know that this must happen in a sealed glass within our furnace, for they are not among our children.

### Concerning the Philosopher’s Stone <note>original: *De lapide Philosophico*</note>

Afterward, following long and steady **decoction** <term>decoction; the process of heating a substance in a liquid or its own moisture to extract its essence or alter its state</term> and management of the fire, the philosophers saw the earth grow and become coarser, and thereafter smaller and less, for the sake of the tempered heat; then they all said: it is a **perfect incineration** <note>original: *perfecta incineratio*; the stage where the matter is reduced to a fine, pure ash</note>, and that was its own name. Therefore **Dandin the Philosopher** <note>likely referring to John Dastin, a 14th-century English alchemist known for his letters on the Stone</note> says: one should extract its power and give it back to drink. **Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of alchemy</note> says the earth shall be soaked with the water; **Morienus** says: Give the thirsty one to drink until the time comes that he has enough of his juice, and in eternity he shall thirst no more.

> Moisten the bed with **Heavenly Dew** and the bride shall conceive a son.

My child shall know and well understand: if you wish to make the **red stone**, you may bring the **white earth** to redness using its **ferment** and by strengthening the **fire**, until it becomes yellow. Once it is perfectly yellow, like **saffron** <note>original: *Crocus*; in alchemy, this usually refers to a fine reddish-yellow powder or the oxide of a metal</note>, then the **Element of Air** <note>original: *Elementum Aeris*</note> has been turned outward. For under the **governance of the fire** <term>governance of fire</term> <note>original: *Regiment des Feuers*; the methodical management of heat intensity throughout the process</note>, which draws and drives out the **Air**, the fire cannot bring forth the **red tincture** unless the fire is strengthened by a good deal until it becomes red. Now that it is red, pour **Paradise Water** <note>a highly distilled alchemical solvent or "mercurial water" used to dissolve and purify the matter</note> over it until it has drunk up all its water and has all become powder. Then govern the fire until the powder becomes white again, like snow; then increase the fire until it is perfectly yellow again, and ever stronger until it becomes red, and then your work is ready and accomplished.

You have seen in this work all **four elements**, each one individually. First you saw **Water** and **Earth**, which were initially manifest, and the **Air** was within them, which you also saw afterward in the yellow color; and now you see the **Fire** in its redness, as it stands on the outside.

Therefore, the **Ancients** spoke truly when they said that our **stone** is made from **four elements**; yet it was still no more than one, and

->### John Isaac Hollandus<-

...plete blackness, and we see it with our own eyes, that all ***Matter*** <note>original: *Materia*</note> becomes as black as pitch. Why does this happen? The fire drives the ***corruption*** <note>original: *Corruption*; meaning the decay or impurities</note> or rot to the top, and it exits the ***Matter*** through the power of the warmth. However, it does not happen with a strong fire, but rather with a gentle fire; thus the ***corruption*** or ***dregs*** <note>original: *Feces*; the solid remains or sediment</note> that are in the ***Ark*** <note>original: *Arca*; the alchemical vessel or container</note> are gently driven to the surface in this way until everything is black.

Therefore *Morienus* <note>A legendary alchemist often cited in medieval texts</note> says: see to it that you govern your fire in such a way that you do not obtain a whiteness before the blackness, or the entire work is spoiled. If whiteness comes before blackness, [it is a failure], so it must be a certain path that the ***corruption*** is driven out by the fire, and in this way the cleansing and ***perfection*** <note>original: *Perfection*</note> must occur. Be cautious in our work, for after long and constant boiling, the heat consumes the ***corruption***, ***dregs***, and blackness, and brings it into another color, and ever another, until it becomes ***perfectly*** white, like snow. This happens gently, so that the ***elements*** <note>original: *Elementa*</note> are not forced, but mildly ***rectified*** <note>original: *rectificiret*; purified or refined</note> of all their impurity. But guard yourselves in every way, as *Morienus* warns, that you do not obtain the redness before the whiteness, for one must not burn our **Stone** in the work. -># Concerning the Philosopher's Stone #<-

Now you might ask, when a thing is thus destroyed, where does the perfection that is within it remain? Read about this in the <term>Plant Kingdom <gloss>original: *Vegetabili*</gloss></term>, Chapter 29. Know this: when a thing has died, whether it be sentient or insentient, the spirit of that **body** <note>original: *Corporis*</note> separates from the thing and goes to its own kind from whence it came, as you will understand in the *Plant Kingdom*. Consider the flame of a fire or coals: the flames heat, the smoke creeps upward, and in this smoke is hidden the spirit of the air, which goes to its own kind; the other **elements** <note>original: *Elementa*</note> should be understood in the same way.

<margin>N 1</margin>

Let this stay in the glass, protected from rain and wind for a long time, and the slimy black **matter** will, in time, become white as snow, and all its stinking odor shall vanish. This is how the nature of the sun works.

For **Moon** <note>original symbol: ☽; referring to Silver</note> has two infirmities <note>original: *Siechthum*, meaning a sickness or defect in the metal's purity</note>, just as other imperfect metals do, but these two infirmities do not reach the innermost root as they do in the other imperfect metals. Thus, arsenic and orpiment are compared to **Theriac** <note>a famous historical medical concoction used as a universal antidote to poison</note>. For when the venom in the Theriac is not prepared, it kills the person; but when it is prepared, it drives the venom out. Arsenic and orpiment act in the same way.

# On the Philosopher's Stone <note>original Latin: *De lapide Philosophico*</note>

Work mentioned regarding the **Moon** <note>original symbol: ☾; referring to Silver</note> is done; then **dissolve** <note>original Latin: *solvirs*</note> it again. Perform this **dissolving** and **coagulating** <note>the process of turning a liquid into a solid or semi-solid state</note> until no **dregs** <note>original Latin: *Feces*</note> remain behind; then the work is fulfilled. Dandin <note>likely an alchemical authority or pseudonym</note> says: unlock that which is enclosed and make it wet; and that which is unlocked, lock it and dry it. Likewise also the coldness of the **Moon**, and you shall find the warmth of the **Sun** <note>original symbol: ☉; referring to Gold</note>, and you shall find the coldness of the Moon <note>original Latin: *Lunæ*</note>.

Now the **Matter** <note>original Latin: *Materia*</note> is ready to extract the **Stone** <note>original Latin: *Lapidem*; the Philosopher's Stone</note>. The matter of Gold should for the most part glow or ascend <note>referring to sublimation, where a solid turns into vapor and rises</note>, and you should take with it all the subtle parts of the **Moon**; nothing should remain in the ascent, or very little—nothing but its subtle parts. For the greater part of the **Moon**, which is coarse, <term>phlegmatic <gloss>referring to the humor of water; here meaning sluggish, heavy, or moist</gloss></term>, and feminine, remains at the bottom.

And the **Sun** alone is subtle and masculine in its parts. When the **Sun** is then dissolved and opened, it glows and rises together because of its great subtlety; but the **Moon** remains lying down below at the bottom, and as of yet, it will not ascend because of its coarseness.

Thus there is an **opposite** <note>original Latin: *contrarium*</note> in these two lights <note>the Sun and Moon, or Gold and Silver</note>: what is the destruction of the one is the advancement and creation of the other. Therefore they belong together in the work, as you well know.

Afterward, **sublime** <note>original: *sublimirt*; to heat a substance until it vaporizes and then becomes solid again</note> this matter in every manner, as is taught in the **White and Red** <note>the two main stages of the Great Work: *albedo* (whiteness) and *rubedo* (redness)</note>. Beware of the air when you open the glass, so that it does not kill you <note>a warning against inhaling toxic metallic or acidic vapors released during the process</note>.

## Multiplication.

To **multiply** <term>original: *Multiplicatio*; the process of increasing the potency or quantity of the Philosopher's Stone</term> your **Stone** in its power, but not in its physical size—that is, so that it shall be elevated in its nobility and **subtlety** <note>its refinement and ability to penetrate other metals</note>—so that it performs 10,000 parts in the **projection** <term>original: *Projection*; the act of casting the Stone upon base metals to transform them into gold or silver</term>. When it has been multiplied, refined, and elevated in its size and power, its projection then performs 1,000,000 parts.

And when you have multiplied the Stone three times and made it subtle in its power, its projection will be without end because of its great subtlety; indeed, the Stone could be multiplied so many times that one would never reach the limit of its projection.

# This is the Book of the Stone
## and its accompanying Projection. <term>Projection: The final stage of the alchemical Great Work, where a small amount of the Philosopher's Stone is "cast upon" a larger mass of molten base metal to transform it into gold or silver</term>

# On the Philosopher’s Stone.

Always cast your **white stone** upon **Tin** <note>original symbol: ♃; Jupiter</note> and not upon other metals, for **Tin** <note>original symbol: ♃</note> is closest to **Silver** <note>original symbol: ☾; Moon</note>, but it is rawer and an "uncooked" body <note>original: "ungekochter Leichnam"; in alchemy, base metals were viewed as "dead" or immature versions of noble metals that needed to be "vitalized" or "ripened"</note>, and the Stone need do nothing else but "fully cook" the **Tin** <note>original symbol: ♃</note>, as I have taught in other places. One could indeed also transmute the other metals into **Silver** <note>original symbol: ☾</note>, but they are much more impure than **Tin** <note>original symbol: ♃</note>, and the **projection** <term>Projection: The final stage of alchemy where the Stone is cast onto molten metal to transform it</term> will not reach as high a grade; furthermore, the Stone would have to drive longer in the fire with the unclean metals before it would yield itself as a king <note>A "king" refers to a perfected, noble metal like gold or silver</note>. Therefore, they do not need to stand so long in the **reverberatory furnace** <note>a furnace that reflects or "reverberates" heat onto the material</note>.

Now that your **calx** <note>the powdery metallic residue</note> of metals is thus opened, take a **flask** <note>original: *Kolben*; a round-bottomed glass vessel</note> that has a wide bottom, and spread the material evenly. **Lute** <note>seal the joints with a clay or paste to make them airtight</note> a large **helm** <note>the top part of a still, also called an alembic</note> to it, set it on the **sublimation furnace** in the **ash bath** <note>a container of ashes used to distribute heat evenly around the glass</note>, attach a **receiver** <note>a vessel to catch the distilled substance</note> to it, and build a fire beneath. At first, let the fire be small, then increase it degree by degree until it begins to glow; then keep it glowing for eight or ten days, yet do not make the fire so strong that the material melts. When the ten days are up, see if any more **mercury** <note>symbolized by ☿</note> is **subliming** <note>the process where a solid turns into vapor and then back to solid on a cool surface</note>. If nothing more comes out, let it cool and remove the helm; there you will find the **mercury** <note>abbreviated as Merc.</note> sublimed, as **white as snow**; save this.

You will find the **salt** or **earth** at the bottom of the glass in the form of a white-gray powder; it is swollen up like a **sponge**, because the **mercury** <note>symbolized by ☿</note> has been drawn out of it. It is with...

### Concerning the Philosophers’ Stone

The process for **silver** <note>symbolized by ☾ or Luna</note>, **copper** <note>symbolized by ♀ or Venus</note>, and **lead** <note>symbolized by ♄ or Saturn</note> is exactly the same, except that the **calx** <note>the powdery metallic residue left after heating</note> of **gold** <note>symbolized by ☉ or Sol</note> must stand for a full 16 or 20 days and must be heated more intensely before the **mercury** <note>symbolized by ☿</note> is released. This is because **gold** does not melt as easily as the other metals; it is much firmer and more stable than **silver** or any other metal.

Now take the salt or "earth" out of the glass, place it into a stone jug, and pour **distilled wine vinegar** over it. Place this in a boiling **water bath** <note>Latin: *balneum*; a vessel of hot water used for gentle, indirect heating</note> and let it stand for 4 to 6 days, stirring it often and keeping it well covered. Then, let it settle and cool; pour off the liquid and save it. Pour fresh **distilled vinegar** onto the **residue** <note>Latin: *feces*; the solid waste remaining at the bottom</note> and return it to the **water bath** for 24 hours, stirring often. Let it settle, then pour this liquid in with the first portion. If you believe there is still some essence left in the **residue**, pour more vinegar over it; if not, throw the residue away, for it is of no use.

Take the vinegar you have poured off and draw it away <note>evaporate it</note> in the **water bath**. The salt will remain at the bottom, clear and snow-white. After this, pour clear, pure water over it and put it back in the **water bath** to let it **dissolve** <note>original German: *aufsolviren*</note>. If any **residue** remains, discard it. **Coagulate** <note>solidify by evaporating the liquid</note> the salt again and dissolve it once more with **common water** <note>Latin: *aqua communi*; plain water</note>. Repeat this process until no more **residue** settles at the bottom. Once this is done, it is ready to perform **Projection** <note>the final alchemical act of casting the substance onto a base metal to transmute it</note> upon **mercury** <note>☿</note>. Extracting the salt from **gold** and other metals is a simpler process than the one just described.

98 days, **copper** <note>symbolized by ♀ or Venus</note> 35 days, because these two must be **reverberated** <note>heated in a furnace where the flame is reflected back onto the material</note> for that long because of their **dregs** <note>original: *Fecum*; the solid impurities or sediment</note>, and they must be heated to a glow slowly so that they do not turn into **glass** <note>the process of vitrification, which would trap the metallic essence</note>, for they do not release their **mercury** <note>here referring to the "spirit" or quicksilver component of the metal</note> easily. If no more will come out, set it back to reverberate for 3 days until nothing more can be extracted.

Once the salt has been worked, perform a **projection** <note>the act of casting a small amount of an alchemical agent onto a larger mass of base metal to transform it</note> onto **mercury** <note>quicksilver</note>, for they **transmute** <note>transform</note> all the mercury since they have little or no spirit left in them. Take mercury, let it become as hot as possible, and throw upon it the **salt of the metals**, 1 part to 100 parts, and then strengthen the fire so that it drives strongly, like **silver** <note>symbolized by ☽ or Luna</note> on the **cupel** <note>original: *Capell*; a shallow, porous bowl used in refining precious metals</note>. Let it stand until it settles into a **regulus** <note>original: *Könige*; a button of pure metal found at the bottom of a crucible after smelting</note>, then quench it immediately as is proper, and you will have fine **silver**.

All salts of the metals, whether they be red or white, only yield **silver** at this stage; however, the **perfect metals** <note>gold and silver</note> perform a higher projection than the **imperfect metals** <note>base metals like lead, tin, or copper</note>. But if they are "reversed" and their innermost essence is brought out, they become **oil** <note>a highly concentrated, liquid alchemical state</note>, and then they all perform a projection for **gold** <note>original: *auf roth* or "onto red"; in alchemy, the "red" stage or "Red Lion" refers to the production of gold</note>. While they previously only affected 100 parts, they now perform a projection on 1000 parts. Previously, one had to throw them only onto mercury, but once they have become **oils**, they perform projection on all metals, as we will teach hereafter.

<margin>Mercury of the Philosophers</margin>
Now we wish to proceed to our work, and first teach how one should extract the <term>Mercury of the Philosophers</term> <note>original: "☿ Philosophorum"; this is not common quicksilver, but a refined spiritual substance extracted from a "body" or mineral.</note>. # Johannis Isaaci Hollandi

->Do not make the fire too hot<- even if it already glows quite brightly; for when you see the signs, the Stone is completed and <term>fix<gloss>Fixed; stable under heat and no longer prone to evaporating or changing.</gloss></term>. I tell you this so that you may maintain moderation in the fire, for if you give it too much heat so that the redness appears before the yellow, you must start over; or if you obtain the white before the black, it is the same result <note>In alchemy, the "Great Work" follows a specific sequence of colors: black (nigredo), white (albedo), yellow (citrinitas), and finally red (rubedo). Skipping a step indicates the fire was too intense, ruining the chemical progression.</note>.

Therefore, it is always better to have too small a fire than one too great, and to proceed only from grade to grade <note>A "grade" refers to a specific level of heat, often categorized by alchemists into four stages of intensity.</note>. As the colors change and intensify, so should one strengthen the fire. This is not only true in this Work, but in all things, for the proper governance of the fire is the second masterpiece in our art; unless the proportion is well observed, all is lost.

Now, proceed. When the <term>Materia<gloss>The physical substance being worked upon in the flask.</gloss></term> is <term>fix</term> and as red as a ruby, take it out and <term>incerirts<gloss>Incerate; the process of "waxing" or softening a dry substance into a waxy consistency by gradually adding liquid.</gloss></term> it with beautiful **Paradise-Water** <note>A powerful alchemical solvent.</note> that has been drawn from **Gold** <term>☉<gloss>The alchemical symbol for the Sun, representing gold.</gloss></term> (just as was said regarding **Silver** <term>☽<gloss>The alchemical symbol for the Moon, representing silver.</gloss></term>). Pour 9 parts of **Paradise-Water** onto 1 part of the **Red Stone**, and seal the glass at the top with strong <term>Luto<gloss>Lute; a specialized clay or paste used to hermetically seal laboratory vessels to prevent the escape of vapors.</gloss></term>. Place it back in the furnace in the ashes and give it heat as if you were keeping **Lead** <term>♄<gloss>The alchemical symbol for Saturn, representing lead.</gloss></term> in a fluid state without driving it off <note>Meaning a gentle, steady heat just above the melting point of lead (roughly 327°C or 621°F), but not hot enough to cause evaporation.</note>, until it has entirely drunk up the **Paradise-Water**. Then it will have become a gray powder, yet more black than gray. Then maintain the fire at that same heat until it becomes truly white; for then

# On the Philosophers' Stone <note>original Latin: "De lapide Philosophico"</note>

Increase your fire significantly until you see the <term>Materia<gloss>The physical substance being worked upon in the flask.</gloss></term> begin to turn yellow; then increase the fire a little more until you see that it is dark yellow, proceeding from grade to grade. Once your powder is entirely brown, like saffron <note>Saffron was a common color reference for the "Citrinitas" or yellowing stage, indicating the work was nearing completion.</note>, such that it can become no yellower, then make your fire significantly stronger until you see the red color emerge. Follow with the fire until it becomes perfectly red, like a ruby. Then rejoice, for the Stone for the Red is completed; let it cool.

Take out half, and leave the other half to be <term>multiplied<gloss>Multiplication is the process of increasing the quantity and the transmutative power of the Stone so that a small amount can transform even more base metal.</gloss></term>. Place what you have taken out into a crucible, let it melt, and pour it into a small glass vial that has been greased with tallow <note>Animal fat was used to grease the mold so the cooling "glass" of the Stone would not stick to the sides.</note>. Pour the Stone into it, and it will be as hard as glass and as red as a ruby. Take 1 part of this and cast it upon 2000 parts of **Lead** <term>♄<gloss>The alchemical symbol for Saturn, representing the base metal lead.</gloss></term>, and it will become the finest **Gold** <term>Sol<gloss>Latin for "Sun," the alchemical name for gold.</gloss></term>, as rich in color as has ever been seen, and it will withstand all tests and examinations; thank God.

## Multiplication of the Red <note>original Latin: "Multiplicatio Rubei"</note>

Afterward, set the other half to be multiplied: for 1 part of the Stone, take 200 parts of your <term>calcined<gloss>Reduced to a fine powder through high heat.</gloss></term> Gold or <term>cemented<gloss>Gold purified by "cementation," a process of heating gold with abrasive salts to remove impurities.</gloss></term> Gold. Dissolve it, precipitate it, wash it, and dry it; afterward, incorporate it into the Stone and place it back into the glass, and pour upon it
